Research & Engineering Lineage · Evolved-DRF

Reliability & Maintainability Engineering

Reliability and maintainability: a required function under stated conditions

Reliability concerns delivery of a declared function over a mission, interval or demand population. Maintainability concerns restoration under specified conditions; supportability concerns the resources, skills, tools and authority needed for that work. The accepted r2 study keeps those functions distinct across fifty-five historical identities and their complete current propositions, profiles and evidence partitions.

The denominator and model are part of the claim

A survival probability, point availability, observed interval availability, recurring-event intensity and failures per demand are different quantities. Two histories can both have 99% observed availability while one has many brief interruptions and another one long outage. The equality supplies no consumer tolerance.

Under suitable finite-mean regenerative cycles, the long-run up-time fraction can be E[U]/(E[U]+E[D]). That does not automatically establish convergence of point availability or justify a particular exponential model. Hands-on repair time can omit diagnosis, logistics and validation; overlapping delays require their actual interval or critical-path accounting.

Redundancy can help without independence—and can add harm

For ideal OR success events A and B with no new interaction failure, P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B∩¬A). A useful added path rescues part of A's failure set; statistical independence is unnecessary for that identity.

In the stipulated example, both paths succeed with probability .89, each alone succeeds in .01, and both fail in .09. Each individual path succeeds .90; the pair succeeds .91 despite positive dependence. The independence shortcut would incorrectly give .99. Adding a genuinely new independent serial controller with reliability .95 changes the architecture's success to .8645. A spare's rescue value and a changed architecture's additional losses must therefore be assessed separately.

Detection is not diagnosis, action or restoration

A second example has sixty signals among one hundred fault opportunities and ninety-nine alarms among 9,900 healthy opportunities. Detection coverage is .60, the false-alarm rate is .01, and positive predictive value is 60/159. Isolation, containment and restoration have different numerators and conditioning sets. A useful signal may still support a harmful automatic action under the actual loss model.

A symptom-level remedy can be adequate without complete causal knowledge. Restoration must nevertheless satisfy its own postcondition: a restart command or restored bytes do not automatically establish a whole mission. Cheap checks can suffice when they actually discriminate the required result.

Capacity, alternatives and evidence limits

Live service headroom is not spare-parts inventory. Bursts, retries, correlated failover and backlog replay compete with service demand. In the stipulated fluid example, capacity is 100 and base demand 90; one extra attempt for 20% of requests raises offered work to 108. This constant-load case cannot drain, but it does not show that every retry is harmful after conditions change.

The thirteen selected pairs yield twenty-six examined directions; the other 2,944 possible non-self directions are unexamined as within-lineage pairs, not rejected. Four configurations preserve direct rebuild, simpler repair/support, supported redundancy and bounded degraded service. Five novelty probes found no new general property identity. Finite constructions, source dependence, access limits and unresolved common-cause inference do not establish realized reliability, a universal reserve percentage or an optimum maintenance policy.

PROPERTY_NAME

Explicit required-function and mission semantics

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Wartime/post-war equipment reliability requirements; mission-success language in military reliability programmes; later dependability standards.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. HARDWARE_RELIABILITY_LINEAGE

  2. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  2. SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

  3. CONVERGENT_PROPERTY

ORIGINAL_FORM

State a numerical reliability objective for an item over a mission time.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

A probability has no engineering meaning until the required function, consumer, conditions, interval and failure threshold are fixed.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

The named system or service function must meet specified performance, timing, state and consequence criteria for the declared consumer.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Failure is non-performance, untimely performance, erroneous performance or performance below the declared threshold—not merely component death.

MECHANISM

Define function, mission/service, modes, performance thresholds, failure scoring, consumer and mission time/demand before modelling or testing.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Any reliability, availability, demonstration, redundancy, recovery or service-level claim that could drive design, release, maintenance or acceptance.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

For low-consequence reversible work, use a direct pass/fail functional check and a short observation window rather than a probabilistic programme.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Stakeholder/consumer criteria, mission phases, state authority, measurable outputs and an agreed scoring rule.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Prevents metric optimisation for a component or proxy while the actual mission/user function fails.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Mission owner, service consumer, operator, maintainer, acceptance authority or risk decision-maker.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Ambiguous verbs; moving thresholds; component-centric scoring; omitted partial failures; disputed responsibility boundaries.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Requirements can be bureaucratic or falsely precise; rare severe consequences can be hidden by an average success definition.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Component survival targets were broadened to mission reliability, functional failure, user journeys and consequence-aware degraded states.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A testable, versioned mission contract that binds required function, mode, profile, environment, interval/demand, degraded acceptance and consumer consequence.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A reliability requirement template is optional; the property is semantic closure on what success and failure mean.

EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE

AWS, Meta and GitLab incidents show that locally alive components can coexist with unavailable or incorrect end functions (SRC-058–SRC-060).

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

No evidence supports a context-free scalar called “reliability” independent of function, conditions and time/demand.

OPEN_QUESTIONS

How should multi-consumer missions aggregate conflicting thresholds without erasing vulnerable or high-consequence users?

disposition

RETAIN_WITH_SCOPE

reason_codes

  1. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

bearer

A specified item or service and its declared required function for a consumer.

proposition

A reliability assertion becomes interpretable when it identifies success/failure, the relevant mission or demand interval and the conditions over which it is asserted.

guard_quantifier

For each asserted reliability estimand, define its event and conditioning domain. This does not require an elaborate mission document for every local operation.

model_domain

Definitions can be internally precise before any field measurement. External reliability requires a correspondence between the event and the actual required function.

mechanism

The definition distinguishes missed function from merely surviving components and supplies the event that tests or observations can count.

consumer_decision

Design acceptance, test scope, service promise or maintenance priority.

positive_scope

Binary directly observed functions and richer phased missions are both admissible.

negative_scope

A written contract alone neither improves a device nor establishes that all affected consumers accept the threshold.

counterexample

A service returns an HTTP response while the requested payment is not committed; its process health is not the user's success event.

criterion

Qualitative: can a reader classify concrete success, failure and permitted degraded cases without silently changing the consumer or denominator?

evidence_refs

  1. F006

  2. F046

  3. F024

evidence_ceiling

Primary normative/practitioner definitions and an analytical necessity of specifying an estimand; no causal effect size for documentation.

remaining_premises

Authority to choose thresholds, actual observability, disputed consumer consequences and correspondence to deployed behavior.

cheap_path_alternatives

For a reversible local operation, name one pass/fail postcondition and check it directly; bound scenarios if probabilities add no decision value.

cost_retirement

Maintain only distinctions used by an actual consumer; retire obsolete mission versions while preserving which version supported prior evidence.

audit_question

What exact function, consumer, interval and failure event does this claim concern, and could a green local signal coexist with failure of that function?

cases

  1. C04

  2. C11

change_note

Preserves native mission semantics while separating model definition, observation and normative acceptance.

PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P002

PROPERTY_NAME

Operational-profile, environment and demand definition

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Life testing and field-data stratification; software operational-profile work in the early 1990s; modern service and mission profiling.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. LIFE_DATA_AND_STATISTICAL_RELIABILITY_LINEAGE

  2. SOFTWARE_RELIABILITY_LINEAGE

  3. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. STATISTICAL_RELIABILITY_ANCESTRY

  2. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  3. DOMAIN_TRANSLATION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Estimate reliability under a specified duty cycle and environment or sample test operations in field-frequency proportion.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Failure probability changes with usage, load, environment, mode, maintenance, software inputs and dependencies.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

The function in ERM-P001 under the actual or deliberately bounded distribution of demands and conditions.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Evidence or design appears reliable under a convenient profile but fails under real frequency, severity, mode transition or rare consequence-important demand.

MECHANISM

Version and measure workloads, mission phases, physical stresses, user classes, duty cycles, dependencies, maintenance states and rare critical operations.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Prediction, demonstration, accelerated testing, software testing, SLO definition, capacity planning, maintenance policy or field-transfer claim.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Use a small set of bounding scenarios when a full probability distribution would not change the decision.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Telemetry or credible mission analysis, stable definitions, sampling weights and explicit treatment of rare high-consequence demands.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Reduces false confidence from laboratory, average-load or dominant-user evidence that excludes the conditions causing failure.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Test planner, reliability analyst, service owner, maintainer, release authority and mission decision-maker.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Stale profiles; survivorship bias; request-weighting that hides users; omitted maintenance/change states; extrapolation beyond observed support.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Profiles can encode current behaviour and suppress novel uses; high-consequence rare events may deserve more weight than frequency implies.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Frequency-only profiles evolved toward stratified, consequence-aware and continuously refreshed exposure models.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A configuration-bound, uncertainty-labelled exposure model that supports both representative sampling and explicit stress/boundary cases.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A workload spreadsheet is optional; the property is evidence about where, how often and under what conditions function is demanded.

reason_codes

  1. NEW_EVIDENCE

  2. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

bearer

An exposure or operational-profile model for a specified population and configuration.

proposition

Reliability estimates and representative tests depend on the input, state, environment and demand distribution to which they refer.

guard_quantifier

For a weighted estimand p=sum(w_i p_i), weights must describe the intended population. Representative frequency sampling does not by itself protect rare high-consequence cases.

model_domain

The weighted-probability identity is mathematical; profile estimation and transport are empirical.

mechanism

Changing weights changes aggregate risk even if every conditional failure probability stays fixed; bounding tests can explore low-frequency mechanisms separately.

consumer_decision

Test allocation, release comparison and interpretation of field rates.

positive_scope

Frequency-weighted use profiles, explicit mission phases and small bounding scenario sets.

negative_scope

No claim that use-proportional testing maximizes all objectives or that yesterday's observed usage defines tomorrow's acceptable use.

counterexample

A release improves the dominant journey and fails a small cohort completely while the aggregate target passes.

criterion

Check population/configuration identity, profile uncertainty, rare-consequence coverage and which changed weights would invalidate the decision.

evidence_refs

  1. F038

  2. F024

  3. F046

evidence_ceiling

Scoped primary technical/practitioner sources plus exact arithmetic; Musa1993 original body remains unexamined and is not credited as fresh proof.

remaining_premises

Representative observation, unobserved states, future drift, desired coverage and the loss function.

cheap_path_alternatives

Use a few justified bounding cases when estimating a detailed distribution cannot affect the decision.

cost_retirement

Profile collection can be costly and privacy-sensitive; retain only justified granularity and refresh when relevant exposure changes.

audit_question

Which inputs, state histories and environments were represented, what is omitted, and does the intended use distribution differ?

cases

  1. C08

  2. C09

change_note

Preserves the native profile requirement and rejects automatic optimization/transport claims.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

PROPERTY

Operational-profile, environment and demand definition

CLAIM

Reliability estimates and representative tests depend on the input, state, environment and demand distribution to which they refer. Guard: For a weighted estimand p=sum(w_i p_i), weights must describe the intended population. Representative frequency sampling does not by itself protect rare high-consequence cases.

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Test allocation, release comparison and interpretation of field rates.

CHEAP_PATH

Use a few justified bounding cases when estimating a detailed distribution cannot affect the decision.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

A release improves the dominant journey and fails a small cohort completely while the aggregate target passes.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.

MATURE_FORM

Reliability estimates and representative tests depend on the input, state, environment and demand distribution to which they refer. Guard: For a weighted estimand p=sum(w_i p_i), weights must describe the intended population. Representative frequency sampling does not by itself protect rare high-consequence cases.

profile_scope

The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY

No single universal conflict; check local cost, consequence, coupling and competing system objectives.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate operational-profile, environment and demand definition? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - What population, denominator, model, confidence, censoring rule and expiry condition bound the reliability claim?

current_audit_questions

  1. Which inputs, state histories and environments were represented, what is omitted, and does the intended use distribution differ?

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P003

PROPERTY_NAME

Explicit complete, partial, intermittent, latent and degraded failure states

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

FMEA/FMECA failure-mode taxonomies, multi-state reliability, maintainability and dependable-computing fault/error/failure distinctions.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. FAILURE_ANALYSIS_LINEAGE

  2. AVAILABILITY_AND_REPAIRABLE_SYSTEMS_LINEAGE

  3. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  2. FAULT_TOLERANCE_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

  3. CONVERGENT_PROPERTY

ORIGINAL_FORM

Classify each item as operating or failed and enumerate failure modes.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Binary up/down states erase partial service, false output, intermittency, dormant standby defects and acceptable degradation.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Required function and quality thresholds for each operating mode, including which reduced capabilities remain acceptable and for how long.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

A harmful state is classified as “up,” or an acceptable degraded state is counted as complete failure, corrupting decisions and metrics.

MECHANISM

Define state space, observable criteria, transitions, dwell limits, latent conditions, false indications and consumer consequences.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Systems with multiple modes, redundancy, standby, partial service, performance thresholds, intermittent faults or hidden protective functions.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

A binary state is sufficient only when the consumer consequence is genuinely binary and the observation tests the complete function.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

State observability, mission criteria, transition rules, timing and authority for accepting/ending degradation.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Enables meaningful availability, diagnostics, degradation and recovery claims instead of uptime theatre.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Operator, mission owner, service consumer, model builder and incident reviewer.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

State explosion; inconsistent scoring; unobservable latent states; “degraded” used to normalise unacceptable service.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Multi-state models can create false precision and obscure simpler decisive thresholds.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Binary life models were supplemented by functional failure, multi-state availability, degraded modes and user-impact measures.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A minimal consequence-relevant state model with explicit observation, entry/exit criteria, allowed duration and treatment of latent states.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A state diagram is optional; the property is unambiguous classification of the states that matter to the mission.

EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE

GitLab’s service was unavailable and lost data while different storage functions had different outcomes; Meta’s DNS servers were locally operational but unreachable (SRC-059, SRC-060).

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

No single multi-state taxonomy transfers without mission-specific thresholds.

OPEN_QUESTIONS

What is the minimum state resolution that preserves consequence without making evidence collection intractable?

APPLICABLE

PROPERTY

Explicit complete, partial, intermittent, latent and degraded failure states

REQUIRED_FUNCTION

Required function and quality thresholds for each operating mode, including which reduced capabilities remain acceptable and for how long.

MISSION_OR_SERVICE

Required function and quality thresholds for each operating mode, including which reduced capabilities remain acceptable and for how long.

OPERATING_PROFILE

Declared demands, workload mix, duty cycle, mode changes and maintenance states.

ENVIRONMENT

Declared physical, software, organisational and dependency environment.

FAILURE_DEFINITION

A harmful state is classified as “up,” or an acceptable degraded state is counted as complete failure, corrupting decisions and metrics.

DEGRADED_ACCEPTABLE_STATE

Only states explicitly accepted by mission/consumer criteria; otherwise none.

MISSION_TIME_OR_DEMAND

Specified interval, number of demands or service-measurement window.

CONSUMER

Operator, mission owner, service consumer, model builder and incident reviewer.

CHEAP_PATH

A binary state is sufficient only when the consumer consequence is genuinely binary and the observation tests the complete function.

MATURE_FORM

A minimal consequence-relevant state model with explicit observation, entry/exit criteria, allowed duration and treatment of latent states.

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Explicit complete, partial, intermittent, latent and degraded failure states

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

A harmful state is classified as “up,” or an acceptable degraded state is counted as complete failure, corrupting decisions and metrics.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

A harmful state is classified as “up,” or an acceptable degraded state is counted as complete failure, corrupting decisions and metrics.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

State observability, mission criteria, transition rules, timing and authority for accepting/ending degradation.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Outcome- or function-relevant observation, not a component heartbeat alone.

CONTROL

Define state space, observable criteria, transitions, dwell limits, latent conditions, false indications and consumer consequences.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodelled combinations, dependence, coverage gaps and changed configuration remain.

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

false

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE

The property does not itself claim redundancy benefit; any redundant implementation must invoke ERM-P008/ERM-P009.

native_id

ERM-P003

current_id

DRF-L2-C003

disposition

RETAIN_NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE

reason_codes

  1. NEW_EVIDENCE

bearer

A state representation of a named function.

proposition

Distinguishing complete, partial, intermittent, latent and accepted degraded states is useful when those distinctions change a consequence or response.

guard_quantifier

Introduce a state only with a discernible meaning and relevant decision. A binary state is adequate when it covers the actual binary function.

model_domain

A state label is a model convention; classification accuracy and duration are observational claims.

mechanism

Separates undetected loss, degraded service and restoration transitions that a single uptime bit can conceal.

consumer_decision

Monitoring, containment, maintenance and return to service.

positive_scope

Minimal binary or multistate descriptions matched to function.

negative_scope

More states do not imply greater reliability or useful precision.

counterexample

Two systems with identical observed availability have different interruption counts and longest outages.

criterion

Each retained state has an entry/exit meaning, consequence and observation rule; unknown latent state remains unknown.

evidence_refs

  1. F009

  2. F046

  3. F024

evidence_ceiling

Taxonomy, historical definitions and constructed distinction; no empirical validation of a specific classifier.

remaining_premises

Reliable observations, allowable degraded duration and consumer interpretation.

cheap_path_alternatives

Keep a direct functional pass/fail check when additional state labels cannot alter an action or interpretation.

cost_retirement

Remove unused state categories; account for classification labor and false alarms.

audit_question

Which materially different failure/degraded states does the metric merge, and are the distinctions actually observable?

cases

  1. C01

  2. C11

change_note

Native minimal-state and cheap-path wording survives independent examination.

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate explicit complete, partial, intermittent, latent and degraded failure states? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version?

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P004

PROPERTY_NAME

System boundary and failure-attribution discipline

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Fault-tree ground rules, RBD success paths, field failure reporting and service dependency analysis.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. FAILURE_ANALYSIS_LINEAGE

  2. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION

  3. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  2. SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

  3. CONVERGENT_PROPERTY

ORIGINAL_FORM

Choose the item under analysis and attribute each observed failure to a component.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Changing the item boundary or excluding dependencies, maintenance, planned windows or user-side effects can manufacture reliability.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

The end-to-end function across all components, services, people and support resources inside the declared responsibility/decision boundary.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

A mission failure is omitted, double-counted or assigned to an external party so that no owner sees the actual system risk.

MECHANISM

Declare analysis boundary, inclusions/exclusions, interfaces, responsibility versus causal attribution, denominator and disputed cases.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

RBD/FTA/FMEA, SLA/SLO, supplier reliability, incident metrics, field-return analysis or cross-organisation service paths.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

For a local reversible decision, state a narrow boundary explicitly and avoid claiming end-to-end reliability.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Dependency inventory, interface contracts, event correlation, shared clocks/identifiers and adjudication rules.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Prevents local optimisation and denominator gaming while preserving causal learning across interfaces.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

System owner, supplier manager, SRE/service owner, maintainer and acceptance authority.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Boundary disputes; “external cause” exclusion; planned-maintenance exclusions; missing user telemetry; ownership confused with causation.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Very broad boundaries make measurement and accountability difficult; too-narrow boundaries make claims irrelevant.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Component attribution evolved toward end-to-end dependency and consumer-consequence accounting while retaining local causal analysis.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A layered boundary model: end-to-end consequence for reliability claims, plus component/dependency attribution for corrective action.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A service map or fault tree is optional; the property is stable scope and transparent exclusions.

PROPERTY

System boundary and failure-attribution discipline

REQUIRED_FUNCTION

The end-to-end function across all components, services, people and support resources inside the declared responsibility/decision boundary.

MISSION_OR_SERVICE

The end-to-end function across all components, services, people and support resources inside the declared responsibility/decision boundary.

OPERATING_PROFILE

Declared demands, workload mix, duty cycle, mode changes and maintenance states.

ENVIRONMENT

Declared physical, software, organisational and dependency environment.

FAILURE_DEFINITION

A mission failure is omitted, double-counted or assigned to an external party so that no owner sees the actual system risk.

DEGRADED_ACCEPTABLE_STATE

Only states explicitly accepted by mission/consumer criteria; otherwise none.

MISSION_TIME_OR_DEMAND

Specified interval, number of demands or service-measurement window.

CONSUMER

System owner, supplier manager, SRE/service owner, maintainer and acceptance authority.

CHEAP_PATH

For a local reversible decision, state a narrow boundary explicitly and avoid claiming end-to-end reliability.

MATURE_FORM

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

System boundary and failure-attribution discipline

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

A mission failure is omitted, double-counted or assigned to an external party so that no owner sees the actual system risk.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

A mission failure is omitted, double-counted or assigned to an external party so that no owner sees the actual system risk.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

Dependency inventory, interface contracts, event correlation, shared clocks/identifiers and adjudication rules.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Outcome- or function-relevant observation, not a component heartbeat alone.

CONTROL

Declare analysis boundary, inclusions/exclusions, interfaces, responsibility versus causal attribution, denominator and disputed cases.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodelled combinations, dependence, coverage gaps and changed configuration remain.

current_claim
native_id

ERM-P004

current_id

DRF-L2-C004

disposition

RETAIN_WITH_SCOPE

reason_codes

  1. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

  2. NEW_EVIDENCE

bearer

A claim boundary and its interfaces, distinct from an organizational blame boundary.

proposition

An internal restoration or component reliability claim may be valid at its stated boundary while a wider consumer function remains failed; attribution and end-to-end consequence should therefore be recorded separately.

guard_quantifier

For each claim, preserve the actual boundary. Do not require every legitimate local claim to prove every external dependency.

model_domain

Local predicates and their conjunction are logical; boundary adequacy and attribution need external evidence.

mechanism

Prevents both overclaiming global success and dismissing a real partial improvement.

consumer_decision

Assign a repair task, describe residual service loss or decide which integration test is still needed.

positive_scope

Layered internal, interface and mission claims.

negative_scope

A dependency's failure is not automatically blame, and widening the boundary indefinitely is not an engineering solution.

counterexample

Valid restored bytes and application state coexist with unavailable credentials and an external counterparty.

criterion

Name the local postcondition, wider receiving criterion and unresolved external premises without collapsing them.

evidence_refs

current_profiles
MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

System boundary and failure-attribution discipline

REQUIRED_FUNCTION

The end-to-end function across all components, services, people and support resources inside the declared responsibility/decision boundary. Current scope: Layered internal, interface and mission claims.

MISSION_OR_SERVICE

The end-to-end function across all components, services, people and support resources inside the declared responsibility/decision boundary. Current scope: Layered internal, interface and mission claims.

OPERATING_PROFILE

Declared demands, workload mix, duty cycle, mode changes and maintenance states.

ENVIRONMENT

Declared physical, software, organisational and dependency environment.

FAILURE_DEFINITION

A mission failure is omitted, double-counted or assigned to an external party so that no owner sees the actual system risk. Current limitation: A dependency's failure is not automatically blame, and widening the boundary indefinitely is not an engineering solution.

DEGRADED_ACCEPTABLE_STATE

Only states explicitly accepted by mission/consumer criteria; otherwise none.

MISSION_TIME_OR_DEMAND

Specified interval, number of demands or service-measurement window.

CONSUMER

Assign a repair task, describe residual service loss or decide which integration test is still needed.

CHEAP_PATH

State a narrow boundary explicitly and avoid unsupported end-to-end language.

MATURE_FORM

An internal restoration or component reliability claim may be valid at its stated boundary while a wider consumer function remains failed; attribution and end-to-end consequence should therefore be recorded separately. Guard: For each claim, preserve the actual boundary. Do not require every legitimate local claim to prove every external dependency.

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

System boundary and failure-attribution discipline

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

A mission failure is omitted, double-counted or assigned to an external party so that no owner sees the actual system risk. Current limitation: A dependency's failure is not automatically blame, and widening the boundary indefinitely is not an engineering solution.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

A mission failure is omitted, double-counted or assigned to an external party so that no owner sees the actual system risk. Current limitation: A dependency's failure is not automatically blame, and widening the boundary indefinitely is not an engineering solution.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

Actual interface contracts, external authority and integration observations.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.

CONTROL

Prevents both overclaiming global success and dismissing a real partial improvement.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodeled combinations, dependence, observation gaps and changed conditions remain possible. A valid bounded containment contribution need not establish diagnosis or complete restoration.

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P005

PROPERTY_NAME

Separate reliability, availability, maintainability, supportability and durability claims

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Post-war reliability/maintainability programmes, repairable-system probability, logistics support and current IEC dependability vocabulary.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. HARDWARE_RELIABILITY_LINEAGE

  2. MAINTAINABILITY_LINEAGE

  3. AVAILABILITY_AND_REPAIRABLE_SYSTEMS_LINEAGE

  4. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  2. MAINTAINABILITY_NATIVE

  3. HYBRID_RESOLUTION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Report MTBF, MTTR and availability as related but distinct quantities.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

High availability can result from frequent fast repairs; high reliability can coexist with slow repair; maintainable design can fail operationally for lack of support.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

A declared mission interval and restoration/support conditions for the item or service.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

A decision substitutes one RAM measure for another and accepts the wrong failure frequency, downtime, repair burden or life limitation.

MECHANISM

Use distinct estimands and state models: no-failure probability, probability of being up, restoration-time distribution, support delay and life/degradation measures.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Any claim using reliability, uptime, availability, MTBF, MTTR, serviceability, durability or operational readiness.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Use direct failure count and downtime decomposition when a full stochastic model is unnecessary; never collapse the labels.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Consistent clocks, failure/restoration definitions, exposure, repair-completion criteria and support-delay data.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Makes design and logistics trade-offs visible and blocks “fast repair” from masquerading as “few failures.”

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Mission planner, operator, maintenance/logistics owner, procurement and service consumer.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Mean measures hide tails; repair clock starts/stops inconsistently; excluded maintenance windows; inherent availability presented as operational availability.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

The vocabulary can become metric-heavy; definitions still need mission consequence and state validity.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Simple component MTBF expanded into mission reliability, inherent/achieved/operational availability, maintainability and supportability.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A small RAM measure set tied to explicit functions, state transitions, total downtime components and decision thresholds.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A RAM dashboard is optional; the property is semantic and denominator integrity across distinct attributes.

GitLab’s long restoration involved diagnosis, backup failure and slow remote infrastructure, demonstrating that total downtime is not simply active repair time (SRC-060).

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

No universal composite “reliability score” preserves all RAM trade-offs.

OPEN_QUESTIONS

Which tail and consumer-weighted measures best complement traditional means without overwhelming decisions?

reason_codes

  1. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

bearer

A specified life, repair cycle or operational support process and the measures defined on it.

proposition

Reliability over a mission, availability over time, maintainability under given resources and total restoration delay answer different questions and cannot be substituted by one mean.

guard_quantifier

Under regenerative cycles with finite positive mean up and down times, long-run time availability is E[U]/(E[U]+E[D]); exponential hazards are sufficient in a two-state Markov model but not necessary for the regenerative ratio.

model_domain

The renewal ratio is an internally derived model result. A finite field estimate needs valid state accounting, cycle assumptions and observed exposure.

mechanism

Separates frequency/duration, active repair and diagnosis/logistics, and prevents a fast local repair metric from hiding slow service recovery.

consumer_decision

Choose prevention, repair, spares or accepted interruption according to the specified consequence.

positive_scope

Finite-mission survival, point availability, interval availability and full delay distributions as separately named quantities.

negative_scope

No general substitution of MTBF for life expectancy, of hands-on repair for downtime, or of a scalar RAM score for separate obligations.

counterexample

Frequent short outages and one long outage yield99% time availability but differ in mission continuity; overlapping diagnosis and spare delivery must not be added twice.

criterion

State units, event/time basis, uptime denominator, delay accounting and assumptions of any formula; inspect tails when the consumer depends on them.

evidence_refs

  1. F006

  2. F007

  3. F013

  4. F005

evidence_ceiling

Definitions and scoped sources plus author's conditional ratio derivation; Lindqvist's read passages explicitly exclude repair durations and are not cited as an availability proof.

remaining_premises

Regeneration, repair quality, resource availability, representative cycles, nonoverlapping time accounting and finite means.

cheap_path_alternatives

Use observed event counts, interval-union downtime and a short delay decomposition when a stochastic model is unnecessary.

cost_retirement

Measure only decision-relevant quantities; do not accumulate dashboards without a receiving decision.

audit_question

Which precise RAM quantity is asserted, under what process assumptions, and which delay or tail could the mean conceal?

cases

change_note

Preserves native distinctions and broadens the valid availability-ratio conditions beyond unnecessary memorylessness.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Separate reliability, availability, maintainability, supportability and durability claims

CLAIM

Reliability over a mission, availability over time, maintainability under given resources and total restoration delay answer different questions and cannot be substituted by one mean. Guard: Under regenerative cycles with finite positive mean up and down times, long-run time availability is E[U]/(E[U]+E[D]); exponential hazards are sufficient in a two-state Markov model but not necessary for the regenerative ratio.

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Choose prevention, repair, spares or accepted interruption according to the specified consequence.

CHEAP_PATH

Use observed event counts, interval-union downtime and a short delay decomposition when a stochastic model is unnecessary.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

Frequent short outages and one long outage yield99% time availability but differ in mission continuity; overlapping diagnosis and spare delivery must not be added twice.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.

MATURE_FORM

Reliability over a mission, availability over time, maintainability under given resources and total restoration delay answer different questions and cannot be substituted by one mean. Guard: Under regenerative cycles with finite positive mean up and down times, long-run time availability is E[U]/(E[U]+E[D]); exponential hazards are sufficient in a two-state Markov model but not necessary for the regenerative ratio.

profile_scope

The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

ERM-P005

POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY

No single universal conflict; check local cost, consequence, coupling and competing system objectives.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate separate reliability, availability, maintainability, supportability and durability claims? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - What population, denominator, model, confidence, censoring rule and expiry condition bound the reliability claim?

[]

current_audit_questions

  1. Which precise RAM quantity is asserted, under what process assumptions, and which delay or tail could the mean conceal?

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P006

PROPERTY_NAME

Systematic failure-mode, effect and propagation challenge

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

1949 military FMECA, later MIL-STD-1629A, FTA and current IEC 60812.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. FAILURE_ANALYSIS_LINEAGE

  2. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  2. SAFETY_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

  3. CONVERGENT_PROPERTY

ORIGINAL_FORM

Enumerate component failure modes and document local, next-higher and end effects in a worksheet.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Nominal architecture descriptions do not reveal plausible loss, erroneous output, timing, interface or propagation paths.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

The function and boundary defined by ERM-P001–P004.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

A plausible mode or propagation path remains uncontrolled because analysis stopped at a component label or single failure.

MECHANISM

Challenge functions and interfaces with plausible modes; trace local-to-end effects, controls, detectability, combinations and evidence for treatment.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Novel/high-consequence functions, complex interfaces, weak field history, design change, repeated incidents or uncertain propagation.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Use a focused “what can fail and what happens next?” review for simple reversible systems; do not require a full worksheet.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Current architecture/configuration, knowledgeable cross-functional participants, explicit ground rules and closure evidence.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Finds single points, latent paths, missing diagnostics and consequence escalation early enough to change design or test.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Designer, reliability engineer, maintainer, tester, operator and acceptance authority.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Checklist copying; unbounded rows; subjective ranks; omission of software/human/dependent combinations; controls listed but unverified.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Bottom-up FMEA can miss interactions and multiple failures; FTA can inherit an incomplete top event and independence assumptions.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Worksheet-centric analysis evolved toward functional, interface, dynamic, dependency and evidence-linked analysis chosen by question.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A proportionate, configuration-bound adversarial analysis that links each important failure path to prevention, detection, containment, recovery or accepted residual risk.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

The FMEA/FMECA table is not the property; systematic challenge and verified closure are.

Major outages repeatedly involve coupled operations, dependencies and recovery paths that a part-only checklist would miss (SRC-058–SRC-062).

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

No method is complete for unknown failure modes or all combinations; analysis must be tested and refreshed.

OPEN_QUESTIONS

How can dynamic/software interactions be covered without producing unreviewable model size?

CONTROL

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodelled combinations, dependence, coverage gaps and changed configuration remain.

disposition

RETAIN_WITH_HISTORICAL_REFINEMENT

reason_codes

  1. NEW_EVIDENCE

  2. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

bearer

A configuration-bound failure-path analysis and the decisions it informs.

proposition

Failure-mode and fault-tree reasoning can expose relevant local, interface and system effects when the modeled modes and propagation logic correspond to the item; a completed representation is not evidence that all paths or controls are valid.

guard_quantifier

For each material modeled path, state its assumptions and consequent prevention, detection, containment, recovery or accepted-risk decision. Unmodeled paths remain possible.

model_domain

Boolean propagation/cut-set results are conditional on the chosen graph; probabilities additionally require a valid joint distribution.

mechanism

Bottom-up effect examination and top-down undesired-event decomposition ask complementary questions; repeated basic events retain one identity.

consumer_decision

Prioritize a design check or correction, confirm an existing control, or justify no action.

positive_scope

Focused causal review, FMEA/FMECA, static/dynamic fault trees or another suitable representation.

negative_scope

Worksheet completion, an ordinal product score or a tiny calculated probability does not establish completeness or effectiveness.

counterexample

Duplicating one power-supply event as two independent leaves spuriously squares its failure probability; an omitted common cause is absent from every computed cut set.

criterion

Can the analyst trace a plausible path, identify the target event, preserve repeated-event identity and show what decision the result supports?

evidence_refs

  1. F045

  2. F046

  3. F048

evidence_ceiling

Primary review/model exposition and historical standard passages, not independent field proof of universal FMEA effectiveness.

remaining_premises

Mode discovery, causality, current configuration, dependency data, severity authority and actual control behavior.

cheap_path_alternatives

A short 'what fails, what happens next, what would we do?' review is adequate when it resolves the live decision.

cost_retirement

Reuse analysis across maintenance/safety where meanings agree; retire stale detail and avoid duplicated worksheets. Historical1629A already advocated tailoring and no-action rationales.

audit_question

Which decisions depend on this analysis, what paths or interactions could be missing, and do shared events remain shared in the calculation?

cases

  1. C02

  2. C04

change_note

Rejects a caricature of historical FMECA as inherently ceremonial; its1980foreword explicitly criticized ineffective isolated analysis.

PROPERTY

Systematic failure-mode, effect and propagation challenge

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

A plausible mode or propagation path remains uncontrolled because analysis stopped at a component label or single failure. Current limitation: Worksheet completion, an ordinal product score or a tiny calculated probability does not establish completeness or effectiveness.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

A plausible mode or propagation path remains uncontrolled because analysis stopped at a component label or single failure. Current limitation: Worksheet completion, an ordinal product score or a tiny calculated probability does not establish completeness or effectiveness.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

Mode discovery, causality, current configuration, dependency data, severity authority and actual control behavior.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.

CONTROL

Bottom-up effect examination and top-down undesired-event decomposition ask complementary questions; repeated basic events retain one identity.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodeled combinations, dependence, observation gaps and changed conditions remain possible. A valid bounded containment contribution need not establish diagnosis or complete restoration.

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P007

PROPERTY_NAME

Single-point and latent-failure exposure control

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

FMECA critical-item lists, fault trees, standby-system analysis and built-in test.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. FAILURE_ANALYSIS_LINEAGE

  2. FAULT_TOLERANT_COMPUTING_LINEAGE

  3. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  2. FAULT_TOLERANCE_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

  3. CONVERGENT_PROPERTY

ORIGINAL_FORM

Identify any single item whose failure causes mission loss and any dormant protective item whose failure is hidden.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

A nominally protected system can have a hidden one-shot failure at a switch, sensor, shared utility, standby channel or maintenance state.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Specified fault tolerance or degraded mission capability under the declared initiating fault set.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

One fault, or one fault plus an undetected latent condition, defeats required function.

MECHANISM

Identify cut sets and latent protective failures; eliminate, isolate, monitor or periodically proof-test them; bound exposure time.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Redundancy, standby, protective functions, emergency equipment, rarely demanded recovery paths and maintenance bypasses.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

For simple systems, trace the end-to-end path once and directly exercise the spare/protective function rather than build a full quantitative tree.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Complete boundary, realistic initial state, demand rate, proof-test interval, detection coverage and restoration plan.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

Credible failure-domain independence, common-cause analysis, standby condition, switchover coverage and state compatibility.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Prevents false redundancy and limits time spent unknowingly one fault away from mission loss.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Architect, maintainer, operator, tester and mission-risk authority.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Hidden bypasses; common sensor/switch; proof test that does not test the whole path; maintenance disables both channels; dormant ageing.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

“Single failure” focus can distract from correlated multi-fault and systemic conditions.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Static single-point lists evolved to minimal cut sets, latent-exposure intervals, dynamic standby and common-cause analysis.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Explicit minimal failure sets including latent states, with elimination or tested detection/repair intervals matched to consequence.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A critical-items list is optional; the property is actual removal or bounded exposure of decisive failure sets.

EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE

GitLab’s failed backup/replication paths and Meta’s simultaneous loss of normal and out-of-band access demonstrate latent and shared recovery-path exposure (SRC-059, SRC-060).

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

A zero single-point-failure count does not prove resilience to dependent combinations.

OPEN_QUESTIONS

How should latent exposure be prioritised when proof testing itself creates maintenance risk?

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Outcome- or function-relevant observation, not a component heartbeat alone.

CONTROL

Identify cut sets and latent protective failures; eliminate, isolate, monitor or periodically proof-test them; bound exposure time.

FAILURE_DOMAINS

INDEPENDENCE_EVIDENCE

COMMON_CAUSE_COUPLINGS

STANDBY_LATENCY_OR_DORMANCY

SWITCHOVER_COVERAGE

Detection, decision, transfer, state synchronisation and post-transfer functional success.

STATE_CONSISTENCY

The takeover state and authority must be current, complete and semantically valid.

DEGRADED_MODE

Declared reduced capability and exit conditions.

TEST_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE

Representative failover/failure tests plus field or incident evidence where available.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

PROPERTY

Single-point and latent-failure exposure control

TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES

One fault, or one fault plus an undetected latent condition, defeats required function.

OBSERVABLES

Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.

DETECTION_COVERAGE

Coverage is stated for an enumerated fault/failure population, operating mode and latency window.

FALSE_ALARM_COST

Unnecessary maintenance, failover, shutdown, operator load or customer disruption.

MISSED_DETECTION_COST

Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.

ISOLATION_RESOLUTION

Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.

AMBIGUITY_GROUPS

Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.

LATENCY

Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.

CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION

Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.

OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION

Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.

RECOVERY_COVERAGE

A detected fault counts only if the prescribed action restores or contains the target failure with known coverage.

MATURE_FORM

Explicit minimal failure sets including latent states, with elimination or tested detection/repair intervals matched to consequence.

disposition

RETAIN_WITH_SCOPE

reason_codes

  1. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

bearer

A required path, standby function or protective function that can fail unnoticed.

proposition

A single required dependency or latent protective failure can defeat a claimed mission or fault tolerance; relevant exposure can be eliminated, detected, repaired or explicitly accepted.

guard_quantifier

Relative to the stated mission and fault model, identify minimal failure sets and latent duration. Single-failure tolerance does not imply tolerance of common causes or all multiple failures.

model_domain

Minimal sets are structural properties of a specified model; latent failure probability and inspection benefit require an observation/repair process.

mechanism

Exercises or checks a dormant function before a real demand, or removes the unique dependency.

consumer_decision

Spare proof test, inspection interval, redesign or accepted outage.

positive_scope

Dormant backups, protective channels and required service paths.

negative_scope

No requirement to eliminate every single point regardless of consequence, feasibility and cost.

counterexample

A spare exists but its credential expired; a component survives while its only power or recovery path is unavailable.

criterion

Identify the demand, dormant state, observable test and consequence of leaving it latent; avoid pretending the test covers other fault classes.

evidence_refs

  1. F046

  2. F045

  3. F017

evidence_ceiling

Formal structural reasoning and scoped historical/incident examples; no generic inspection interval is estimated.

remaining_premises

Test sensitivity, induced harm, demand rate, repair capability and relevant common causes.

cheap_path_alternatives

Trace the actual path once and exercise the protective function directly; accept a low-consequence single point explicitly.

cost_retirement

Testing itself consumes spare life and maintenance attention; retire a proof test when the protected demand or mechanism is removed.

audit_question

What required or dormant function can fail silently, how long could it remain failed, and which tested demand does the check represent?

cases

  1. C04

change_note

Retains the native insight without universal elimination or testing quotas.

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.

CONTROL

FAILURE_DOMAINS

Physical, power, network, control-plane, state, software, supplier, operator and maintenance domains.

INDEPENDENCE_EVIDENCE

Address actual shared causes and the joint event law. Statistical independence is required only by formulas or claims that use it; dependent paths may still provide a positive rescue increment. Copy count or labels alone do not establish separation.

COMMON_CAUSE_COUPLINGS

DEGRADED_MODE

Declared reduced capability and exit conditions.

TEST_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE

Evidence appropriate to the stated protection claim, including a direct deterministic result or a model at its exact premises where adequate. A general architecture or field-rate claim needs correspondingly broader evidence; no universal live-test or field-study bundle is imposed.

native_id

ERM-P007

POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY

No single universal conflict; check local cost, consequence, coupling and competing system objectives.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate single-point and latent-failure exposure control? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - Are the supposed redundant channels actually separate failure domains, and is detection, switchover, state transfer and degraded capacity covered? - Which enumerated failures can the diagnostic detect and isolate within the required latency, and what are the false-positive and false-negative costs?

current_direction_ids

[]

current_audit_questions

  1. What required or dormant function can fail silently, how long could it remain failed, and which tested demand does the check represent?

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P008

PROPERTY_NAME

Common-cause, common-mode and correlated-dependency analysis

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Nuclear and aerospace common-cause analysis, diversity debates, multiversion software experiments and cloud dependency failures.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. FAULT_TOLERANT_COMPUTING_LINEAGE

  2. FAILURE_ANALYSIS_LINEAGE

  3. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION

  4. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  2. FAULT_TOLERANCE_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

  3. DOMAIN_TRANSLATION

  4. HYBRID_RESOLUTION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Apply a beta factor or common-cause event category to redundant components.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Nominal parallel paths share specification, design, environment, power, control, state, supplier, maintenance, deployment or operator causes.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Continued or degraded required function after the claimed fault set.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Several “independent” elements fail together or sequentially from a shared coupling, invalidating the parallel reliability calculation.

MECHANISM

Enumerate failure domains and coupling factors; seek empirical CCF data; model dependence; separate shared controls; test correlated scenarios; reduce concentration.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Any redundancy, multi-region, multi-vendor, diverse implementation, backup, standby or third-party dependency claim.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

When independence cannot be supported, treat copies as one failure domain for the decision and avoid precision theatre.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Architecture/dependency visibility, configuration/supplier data, incident linkage and credible dependence parameters or conservative bounds.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

Credible failure-domain independence, common-cause analysis, standby condition, switchover coverage and state compatibility.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Avoids orders-of-magnitude overstatement of redundancy benefit and exposes hidden ecosystem concentration.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Architect, reliability modeller, service owner, procurement/supplier manager and mission-risk authority.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Unobserved coupling; common specification; shared update; shared operator; correlated maintenance; regional/control-plane dependence; sparse CCF data.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

CCF parameters are uncertain and domain-specific; pessimistic bounding can erase economically useful redundancy.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Assumed independence evolved to explicit failure-domain, beta/alpha-factor, diversity and correlated-dependency treatment.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A qualitative-plus-quantitative coupling argument that states what is shared, what is separated, the evidence for residual dependence and consequences if the assumption fails.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A “multi-AZ” label or beta-factor entry is not the property; credible domain separation and dependence evidence are.

Meta’s backbone/DNS/tool coupling, AWS’s S3 dependency fan-out and CrowdStrike’s homogeneous update propagation provide direct incident support (SRC-058, SRC-059, SRC-061, SRC-062).

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

Redundancy still pays when failure domains and transfer paths are credibly separated; the criticism is of assumed independence, not redundancy itself.

OPEN_QUESTIONS

FAILURE_DOMAINS

INDEPENDENCE_EVIDENCE

COMMON_CAUSE_COUPLINGS

Specification, design, implementation, environment, supplier, maintenance, configuration and operational coupling.

STANDBY_LATENCY_OR_DORMANCY

Dormant faults, activation delay and cold/warm/hot readiness are measured when applicable.

Detection, decision, transfer, state synchronisation and post-transfer functional success.

Declared reduced capability and exit conditions.

Representative failover/failure tests plus field or incident evidence where available.

A qualitative-plus-quantitative coupling argument that states what is shared, what is separated, the evidence for residual dependence and consequences if the assumption fails.
