[]

current_audit_questions

  1. Could false or late action erase the detector's benefit, and which assumptions make the policy better than a simpler check?

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P014

PROPERTY_NAME

Graceful degradation with explicit mission priorities

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Fail-soft/fail-operational computing, multi-state reliability, survivability and service load shedding.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. FAULT_TOLERANT_COMPUTING_LINEAGE

  2. AVAILABILITY_AND_REPAIRABLE_SYSTEMS_LINEAGE

  3. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION

  4. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. FAULT_TOLERANCE_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

  2. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  3. DOMAIN_TRANSLATION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Continue with reduced throughput or disabled noncritical functions after faults.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Binary shutdown wastes residual capability, but uncontrolled “keep running” can hide unsafe, corrupt or inequitable service.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Preserve prioritised critical function within degraded performance, time and consequence limits until repair/recovery or safe stop.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

The degraded state violates unstated dependencies, hides data loss, starves a user class, exceeds duration or cannot be exited.

MECHANISM

Predefine capability tiers, priorities, admission/load shedding, observability, annunciation, time limits, exit/escalation and recovery tests.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Capacity loss, partial dependency failure, redundancy exhaustion or missions where some function is better than none.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Stop safely when degraded operation has no defensible acceptance criteria or adds greater consequence than interruption.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Mission prioritisation, state model, resource reservation, independent observability, operator/user communication and recovery path.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Converts residual resources into protected critical service while bounding hidden deterioration.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Mission owner, user populations, operator and incident commander.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Silent quality erosion; overload of remaining capacity; untested feature interactions; priority inversion; indefinite degraded mode.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

“Graceful” is value-laden; degradation may shift harm to less visible consumers or conflict with safety/security constraints.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Fail-soft hardware evolved toward mission-tiered service, load shedding, partial availability and explicit degraded-state SLOs.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A tested degradation contract specifying protected functions, sacrificed functions, consumer impact, observability, duration and exit criteria.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A feature flag or “degraded mode” label is not the property; controlled consequence and exit are.

PROPERTY

Graceful degradation with explicit mission priorities

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

LOCAL_EFFECT

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

END_EFFECT

The degraded state violates unstated dependencies, hides data loss, starves a user class, exceeds duration or cannot be exited.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

LATENT_CONDITION

DETECTION

CONTROL

Predefine capability tiers, priorities, admission/load shedding, observability, annunciation, time limits, exit/escalation and recovery tests.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodelled combinations, dependence, coverage gaps and changed configuration remain.

PROPERTY

INITIATING_FAILURE

RECOVERY_ACTION

Predefine capability tiers, priorities, admission/load shedding, observability, annunciation, time limits, exit/escalation and recovery tests.

AUTHORITY_SOURCE

CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE

RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND

RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND

Explicit time-to-restoration bound including diagnosis, logistics, repair and validation.

STATE_RECONCILIATION

Resolve divergent, stale, partial or replayed state before authoritative service resumes.

FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS

Preserve prioritised critical function within degraded performance, time and consequence limits until repair/recovery or safe stop.

DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS

Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.

DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS

Critical dependencies and capacity are verified rather than assumed from local restart.

VALIDATION

Independent end-to-end functional and state checks under representative demand.

RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY

Named human or automated authority with explicit acceptance criteria.

ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK

A bounded fallback when restoration validation fails or the original cause persists.

MATURE_FORM

A tested degradation contract specifying protected functions, sacrificed functions, consumer impact, observability, duration and exit criteria.

DISPOSITION_RATIONALE

native_id

ERM-P014

current_id

DRF-L2-C014

disposition

RETAIN_WITH_CONSUMER_SCOPE

reason_codes

  1. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

bearer

A degraded operating state and its affected consumers.

proposition

A reduced function can be a valid protected outcome when its content, duration and consequences meet the declared acceptance criterion; continued responsiveness alone is insufficient.

guard_quantifier

For each degraded mode, specify preserved and sacrificed functions, relevant demand/capacity, duration and exit. The chosen criterion needs appropriate authority.

model_domain

Logical compatibility with a declared contract can be checked; acceptance of consequences and actual transition behavior need outside evidence.

mechanism

Restricts work or substitutes a lesser service to preserve a more important bounded function.

consumer_decision

Load shedding, stale read, feature disablement, manual fallback or stopping.

positive_scope

Useful partial operation without full normal functionality.

negative_scope

No assumption that every fast fallback is acceptable or that an aggregate metric represents affected minorities.

counterexample

C11's120-second stale search result meets its300-second allowance; an equally responsive payment fallback without authoritative balance violates its contract.

criterion

Check the actual reduced output against explicit constraints and inspect the consumers who bear the sacrificed function.

evidence_refs

  1. F043

  2. F024

  3. F017

evidence_ceiling

Primary mechanisms/practice and a constructed contract comparison; no universal mission priority.

remaining_premises

Transition reliability, integrity, authority, capacity, observation and safe exit.

cheap_path_alternatives

A simple restriction and clear status may suffice. Stop when the particular continuation is unsupported and the stopping consequence is acceptable.

cost_retirement

Degraded modes need maintenance and can conceal chronic loss; retire one when its protected use or validity disappears.

audit_question

What exactly survives, who loses which function, for how long, and what evidence makes that reduction acceptable?

cases

  1. C09

  2. C11

change_note

Retains the native consumer-sensitive property without treating every degradation as an obligation.

MISSION_OR_SERVICE

OPERATING_PROFILE

FAILURE_DEFINITION

DEGRADED_ACCEPTABLE_STATE

MISSION_TIME_OR_DEMAND

Specified interval, number of demands or service-measurement window.

CONSUMER

Load shedding, stale read, feature disablement, manual fallback or stopping.

CHEAP_PATH

A simple restriction and clear status may suffice. Stop when the particular continuation is unsupported and the stopping consequence is acceptable.

MATURE_FORM

A reduced function can be a valid protected outcome when its content, duration and consequences meet the declared acceptance criterion; continued responsiveness alone is insufficient. Guard: For each degraded mode, specify preserved and sacrificed functions, relevant demand/capacity, duration and exit. The chosen criterion needs appropriate authority.

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Graceful degradation with explicit mission priorities

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

The degraded state violates unstated dependencies, hides data loss, starves a user class, exceeds duration or cannot be exited. Current limitation: No assumption that every fast fallback is acceptable or that an aggregate metric represents affected minorities.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

The degraded state violates unstated dependencies, hides data loss, starves a user class, exceeds duration or cannot be exited. Current limitation: No assumption that every fast fallback is acceptable or that an aggregate metric represents affected minorities.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

Transition reliability, integrity, authority, capacity, observation and safe exit.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.

CONTROL

Restricts work or substitutes a lesser service to preserve a more important bounded function.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodeled combinations, dependence, observation gaps and changed conditions remain possible. A valid bounded containment contribution need not establish diagnosis or complete restoration.

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

false

PROFILE_TYPE

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE

REASON

The property does not itself claim redundancy benefit; any redundant implementation must invoke ERM-P008/ERM-P009.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

false

PROFILE_TYPE

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE

REASON

The candidate is not a diagnostic claim; outcome observation may still be required by its evidence profile.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Graceful degradation with explicit mission priorities

INITIATING_FAILURE

The degraded state violates unstated dependencies, hides data loss, starves a user class, exceeds duration or cannot be exited. Current limitation: No assumption that every fast fallback is acceptable or that an aggregate metric represents affected minorities.

RECOVERY_ACTION

Restricts work or substitutes a lesser service to preserve a more important bounded function.

AUTHORITY_SOURCE

State/configuration identity and the actual authority relevant to the action or claim. A pure model has no external action authority; a bounded internal restore does not by itself establish authority to resume a wider service.

CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE

Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.

RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND

State/data loss bound where the function depends on preserved state; explicitly state a nontrigger for stateless or directly reconstructible functions.

RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND

The declared restoration interval or bound, if the claim requires one. Distinguish detection, waiting, logistics, repair and validation and avoid summing overlapping intervals.

STATE_RECONCILIATION

Reconcile the state required by the named restored function. Broader divergent or external state may remain an explicit residual; authoritative wider service requires its own relevant conditions.

FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS

Preserve prioritised critical function within degraded performance, time and consequence limits until repair/recovery or safe stop. Current scope: Useful partial operation without full normal functionality.

DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS

Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.

DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS

Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.

VALIDATION

An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.

RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY

Keep proof of the postcondition separate from actual permission to resume consequential service. Name the relevant decision maker or rule when applicable.

ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK

A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.

MATURE_FORM

A reduced function can be a valid protected outcome when its content, duration and consequences meet the declared acceptance criterion; continued responsiveness alone is insufficient. Guard: For each degraded mode, specify preserved and sacrificed functions, relevant demand/capacity, duration and exit. The chosen criterion needs appropriate authority.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE

REASON

profile_scope

The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY

Continuity and reduced capability versus hidden unacceptable or unsafe degradation.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate graceful degradation with explicit mission priorities? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - Does recovery close on independently checked required function, state and dependency postconditions rather than process restart or procedure completion?

current_direction_ids

[]

current_audit_questions

  1. What exactly survives, who loses which function, for how long, and what evidence makes that reduction acceptable?

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P015

PROPERTY_NAME

Contextual selection of fail-safe, fail-stop and fail-operational objectives

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Protective engineering, fail-stop computing, fail-operational aerospace/transport systems and high-availability services.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. FAULT_TOLERANT_COMPUTING_LINEAGE

  2. DOMAIN_SPECIFIC

  3. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. SAFETY_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

  2. FAULT_TOLERANCE_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

  3. UNRESOLVED_TENSION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Choose either a safe state on failure or continued operation through redundancy.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

“Keep running” and “stop safely” protect different consequences and can conflict under uncertain state.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

The action after fault must minimise mission/consumer consequence under the applicable safety, integrity, availability and recoverability priorities.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

A universal availability objective continues corrupt/unsafe operation, or a universal stop policy destroys a time-critical mission that could tolerate degradation.

MECHANISM

Perform consequence- and mode-specific objective selection; define trigger, authority, state confidence, tolerated duration and fallback.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Functions where interruption and continued erroneous operation have materially different consequences.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Default to a simple safe stop for reversible low-consequence work when continued correctness cannot be established.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Consequence model, state observability, independent protection, degraded criteria and cross-discipline constraints.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Prevents reliability optimisation from overriding more important mission consequences.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Mission authority, operator, affected users and cross-functional assurance owners.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Ambiguous safe state; unsafe latent degradation; failover to corrupt state; emergency shutdown causes cascading loss.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

No reliability-only rule resolves the value trade-off; evidence from one domain cannot set another domain’s objective.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Binary slogans evolved toward mode- and consequence-specific state machines with fail-operational intervals and escalation to stop.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A source-grounded, explicitly prioritised transition policy rather than a generic “always available” or “always fail safe” rule.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A “fail-safe” label is not the property; the consequence-based transition and evidence are.

APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Contextual selection of fail-safe, fail-stop and fail-operational objectives

REQUIRED_FUNCTION

The action after fault must minimise mission/consumer consequence under the applicable safety, integrity, availability and recoverability priorities.

MISSION_OR_SERVICE

The action after fault must minimise mission/consumer consequence under the applicable safety, integrity, availability and recoverability priorities.

OPERATING_PROFILE

Declared demands, workload mix, duty cycle, mode changes and maintenance states.

ENVIRONMENT

Declared physical, software, organisational and dependency environment.

FAILURE_DEFINITION

A universal availability objective continues corrupt/unsafe operation, or a universal stop policy destroys a time-critical mission that could tolerate degradation.

DEGRADED_ACCEPTABLE_STATE

Only states explicitly accepted by mission/consumer criteria; otherwise none.

MISSION_TIME_OR_DEMAND

Specified interval, number of demands or service-measurement window.

CONSUMER

Mission authority, operator, affected users and cross-functional assurance owners.

CHEAP_PATH

Default to a simple safe stop for reversible low-consequence work when continued correctness cannot be established.

MATURE_FORM

A source-grounded, explicitly prioritised transition policy rather than a generic “always available” or “always fail safe” rule.

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Contextual selection of fail-safe, fail-stop and fail-operational objectives

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

A universal availability objective continues corrupt/unsafe operation, or a universal stop policy destroys a time-critical mission that could tolerate degradation.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

A universal availability objective continues corrupt/unsafe operation, or a universal stop policy destroys a time-critical mission that could tolerate degradation.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

Consequence model, state observability, independent protection, degraded criteria and cross-discipline constraints.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Outcome- or function-relevant observation, not a component heartbeat alone.

CONTROL

Perform consequence- and mode-specific objective selection; define trigger, authority, state confidence, tolerated duration and fallback.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodelled combinations, dependence, coverage gaps and changed configuration remain.

current_id

DRF-L2-C015

disposition

RETAIN_CONTEXT_DEPENDENT

reason_codes

  1. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

bearer

A transition policy for a named system and consequence domain.

proposition

Fail-stop, fail-safe and fail-operational goals are contextual alternatives; reliability measures alone cannot choose among their consequences.

guard_quantifier

Condition any preferred transition on the actual required function, harm of continuation, harm of interruption and governing authority. A state called 'safe' needs a domain-specific argument.

model_domain

A transition can be specified mathematically; safety, security or mission acceptance is not implied by a reliability objective.

mechanism

Selects which function or resource is sacrificed to avoid a more consequential failure.

consumer_decision

Continue with bounded loss, isolate, stop or transfer control.

positive_scope

Simple stop for appropriate reversible work and bounded continued operation for missions that require it.

negative_scope

No universal always-stop, always-retry or always-available rule.

counterexample

Stopping a dispensable batch job can prevent bad output; removing a continuously required function can itself be the top event.

criterion

Compare the specified consequences of each transition and identify which authority accepts the trade-off.

evidence_refs

  1. F009

  2. F006

  3. F045

evidence_ceiling

Taxonomic/conditional reasoning; no domain certification, current legal determination or application-specific safety analysis.

remaining_premises

Actual hazards, protected obligations, authority and verified transition behavior.

cheap_path_alternatives

Use the simplest supported transition; do not introduce elaborate fail-operational machinery without a protected mission.

cost_retirement

Transition controls can themselves fail and consume resources. Revisit them when the mission or surrounding obligations change.

audit_question

Is stopping actually acceptable here, is continued operation acceptable, and who can decide the remaining trade-off?

cases

  1. C11

change_note

Native context dependence survives; the cheap stop path remains conditional rather than universal.

OPERATING_PROFILE

Declared demands, workload mix, duty cycle, mode changes and maintenance states.

ENVIRONMENT

Declared physical, software, organisational and dependency environment.

FAILURE_DEFINITION

A universal availability objective continues corrupt/unsafe operation, or a universal stop policy destroys a time-critical mission that could tolerate degradation. Current limitation: No universal always-stop, always-retry or always-available rule.

DEGRADED_ACCEPTABLE_STATE

Only states explicitly accepted by mission/consumer criteria; otherwise none.

MISSION_TIME_OR_DEMAND

Specified interval, number of demands or service-measurement window.

LOCAL_EFFECT

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

A universal availability objective continues corrupt/unsafe operation, or a universal stop policy destroys a time-critical mission that could tolerate degradation. Current limitation: No universal always-stop, always-retry or always-available rule.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

DEPENDENCIES

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

LATENT_CONDITION

DETECTION

Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.

native_id

ERM-P015

POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY

Fail-operational continuity versus fail-safe/fail-stop containment.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate contextual selection of fail-safe, fail-stop and fail-operational objectives? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version?

current_direction_ids

[]

current_audit_questions

  1. Is stopping actually acceptable here, is continued operation acceptable, and who can decide the remaining trade-off?

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

PROPERTY_NAME

Recovery closes on required function and state postconditions

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Repairable-system restoration, recovery blocks, high-availability operations, recovery-oriented computing and modern reconstitution guidance.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. AVAILABILITY_AND_REPAIRABLE_SYSTEMS_LINEAGE

  2. FAULT_TOLERANT_COMPUTING_LINEAGE

  3. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION

  4. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  2. FAULT_TOLERANCE_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

  3. DOMAIN_TRANSLATION

  4. HYBRID_RESOLUTION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Count repair complete when the failed component is returned to an “up” state.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Restart, failover or repair may leave stale/corrupt state, unavailable dependencies, insufficient capacity or the initiating common cause.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Re-establish the ERM-P001 required function, authoritative state and dependency readiness within the declared restoration bound.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Process starts but user/mission function is wrong, incomplete, too slow, unauthorised or vulnerable to immediate recurrence.

MECHANISM

Define recovery source/authority, reconcile state, verify dependencies/capacity, perform independent end-to-end functional checks and control return to service.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Restart, retry, failover, rollback, restore, rebuild, repair, workaround or disaster recovery.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

For stateless, low-consequence functions, a direct end-to-end transaction after restart may be sufficient.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Valid source, diagnosis/containment, state semantics, acceptance criteria, independent observability and fallback.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Prevents “green after restart” from being mistaken for restoration and reduces recurrent/corrupt recovery.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Operator, incident commander, mission owner, user and return-to-service authority.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Stale replica; incomplete replay; hidden dependency down; undercapacity; recurring trigger; invalid backup; monitor shares fault.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Exhaustive post-recovery validation can delay urgent service; checks must be risk- and time-proportionate.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Repair completion evolved from component-up to state-, dependency-, consumer- and mission-valid restoration.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A recovery case with explicit preconditions, authoritative state, functional/data/dependency postconditions, independent validation and fallback.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A closed incident or successful command is not the property; observed re-establishment of required function is.

bearer

A recovery operation and a declared local or mission postcondition.

proposition

Recovery success should be stated as the postcondition actually re-established, with unresolved external effects and dependencies separately retained.

guard_quantifier

A command exit status is evidence only for its defined operation. A stronger functional claim needs checks adequate to that function; complete elimination of every latent cause is not required to establish a bounded restoration.

model_domain

Postcondition satisfaction can be a logical/functional result. Future reliability and external reconciliation remain additional claims.

mechanism

Restores useful state/function and checks the receiving criterion rather than equating procedure completion with success.

consumer_decision

Resume a local operation, restore wider service, remain degraded, investigate or stop.

positive_scope

Internal state restoration, partial service recovery and full mission return when each has adequate evidence.

negative_scope

No blanket requirement for exhaustive validation, independent reviewers or global causal closure before any partial restoration counts.

counterexample

C04's internal consistency holds while credentials and an external counterparty remain unavailable; both facts are preserved.

criterion

State precondition, postcondition, observation oracle, residual effects, uncertainty and the scope of return-to-service authority.

evidence_ceiling

Architecture/taxonomy and operator account; no restoration exercise on a deployed system was performed.

remaining_premises

State authority, consistency, compatibility, valid oracle, relevant dependencies and accepted residual risk.

cheap_path_alternatives

For a simple stateless function, one direct transaction may establish the bounded claim; replace/rebuild may be cheaper than state repair.

cost_retirement

Validation time can delay useful recovery. Choose checks that discriminate the asserted result and avoid mandatory unrelated controls.

audit_question

Which postcondition is now true, what observation supports it, and which wider functions or irreversible effects remain unresolved?

change_note

Scopes the native required-function closure to the claim actually made; independent validation is a risk-sensitive technique, not an unconditional ritual.

PROPERTY

INITIATING_FAILURE

Process starts but user/mission function is wrong, incomplete, too slow, unauthorised or vulnerable to immediate recurrence. Current limitation: No blanket requirement for exhaustive validation, independent reviewers or global causal closure before any partial restoration counts.

RECOVERY_ACTION

Restores useful state/function and checks the receiving criterion rather than equating procedure completion with success.

AUTHORITY_SOURCE

State/configuration identity and the actual authority relevant to the action or claim. A pure model has no external action authority; a bounded internal restore does not by itself establish authority to resume a wider service.

CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE

Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.

RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND

State/data loss bound where the function depends on preserved state; explicitly state a nontrigger for stateless or directly reconstructible functions.

RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND

The declared restoration interval or bound, if the claim requires one. Distinguish detection, waiting, logistics, repair and validation and avoid summing overlapping intervals.

STATE_RECONCILIATION

Reconcile the state required by the named restored function. Broader divergent or external state may remain an explicit residual; authoritative wider service requires its own relevant conditions.

FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS

Re-establish the ERM-P001 required function, authoritative state and dependency readiness within the declared restoration bound. Current scope: Internal state restoration, partial service recovery and full mission return when each has adequate evidence.

DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS

Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.

DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS

Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.

VALIDATION

An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.

RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY

Keep proof of the postcondition separate from actual permission to resume consequential service. Name the relevant decision maker or rule when applicable.

ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK

A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.

MATURE_FORM

Recovery success should be stated as the postcondition actually re-established, with unresolved external effects and dependencies separately retained. Guard: A command exit status is evidence only for its defined operation. A stronger functional claim needs checks adequate to that function; complete elimination of every latent cause is not required to establish a bounded restoration.

ERM-P016

POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY

Restoration speed versus diagnostic confidence, state correctness and evidence preservation.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate recovery closes on required function and state postconditions? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - Which enumerated failures can the diagnostic detect and isolate within the required latency, and what are the false-positive and false-negative costs? - Does recovery close on independently checked required function, state and dependency postconditions rather than process restart or procedure completion?

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P017

PROPERTY_NAME

Backup, restore and reconstitution paths must be exercised and validated

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Data backup/contingency practice, disaster recovery and current NIST restore/reconstitution guidance.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MAINTAINABILITY_LINEAGE

  2. AVAILABILITY_AND_REPAIRABLE_SYSTEMS_LINEAGE

  3. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION

  4. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. MAINTAINABILITY_NATIVE

  2. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION

  3. HYBRID_RESOLUTION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Maintain a backup copy and a recovery plan.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Copies can be absent, stale, corrupt, inaccessible, incompatible, contaminated or impossible to restore within field constraints.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Restore required data/state and application function to a trusted, current-enough configuration within RPO/RTO and consequence limits.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Backup job reports success but restore cannot complete, recovered data is inconsistent, required tools/docs are unavailable or the same cause contaminates sources.

MECHANISM

Inventory sources, isolate/protect them, verify integrity/freshness, rehearse non-production restore, validate application semantics and reconstitution logistics.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Any claim of backup, disaster recovery, spare image, replicated state, rebuild-from-code or clean-room recovery.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

For reproducible stateless artefacts, verify rebuild and one functional check instead of elaborate backup infrastructure.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Configuration manifests, credentials, tools, dependencies, capacity, state consistency, acceptance criteria and staff capability.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Converts backup existence into demonstrated recoverability and exposes hidden RPO/RTO/support gaps.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Service/data owner, operator, mission continuity authority and affected users.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Silent backup failure; restore never tested; missing encryption key; version mismatch; partial database; dependent identity/DNS unavailable; contaminated image.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Frequent full rehearsals are costly and can create production risk; representative, isolated exercises and cheaper checks should be chosen by decision value.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Backup media inventory evolved toward recurring restore, application/state validation, clean reconstitution and dependency/tool readiness.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A periodically refreshed restore/reconstitution demonstration closing on functional and state postconditions for the current configuration.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A backup icon, policy or DR document is not the property; a valid exercised recovery path is.

APPLICABLE

PROPERTY

Backup, restore and reconstitution paths must be exercised and validated

INITIATING_FAILURE

Backup job reports success but restore cannot complete, recovered data is inconsistent, required tools/docs are unavailable or the same cause contaminates sources.

RECOVERY_ACTION

Inventory sources, isolate/protect them, verify integrity/freshness, rehearse non-production restore, validate application semantics and reconstitution logistics.

AUTHORITY_SOURCE

The designated current configuration/state authority and authorised operator or controller.

CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE

Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.

RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND

Explicit allowed state/data loss or “none” for state-continuous functions.

RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND

Explicit time-to-restoration bound including diagnosis, logistics, repair and validation.

STATE_RECONCILIATION

Resolve divergent, stale, partial or replayed state before authoritative service resumes.

FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS

Restore required data/state and application function to a trusted, current-enough configuration within RPO/RTO and consequence limits.

DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS

Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.

DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS

Critical dependencies and capacity are verified rather than assumed from local restart.

VALIDATION

Independent end-to-end functional and state checks under representative demand.

RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY

Named human or automated authority with explicit acceptance criteria.

ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK

A bounded fallback when restoration validation fails or the original cause persists.

MATURE_FORM

A periodically refreshed restore/reconstitution demonstration closing on functional and state postconditions for the current configuration.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Backup, restore and reconstitution paths must be exercised and validated

CLAIM

A periodically refreshed restore/reconstitution demonstration closing on functional and state postconditions for the current configuration.

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Exact hardware, software, data, model, dependency and procedure versions.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Predeclared sampling/censoring, failure scoring, exposure and stopping rules.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage and representativeness are explicit.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Intervals, posterior uncertainty or bounded qualitative confidence; point estimates alone are insufficient.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Claim coverage is limited to tested/observed failure modes, environments and paths.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Service/data owner, operator, mission continuity authority and affected users.

CHEAP_PATH

For reproducible stateless artefacts, verify rebuild and one functional check instead of elaborate backup infrastructure.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

A single successful restore does not establish all future restores, configurations or correlated disaster conditions.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Evidence expires when configuration, profile, environment, support organisation or dependencies materially change.

MATURE_FORM

A periodically refreshed restore/reconstitution demonstration closing on functional and state postconditions for the current configuration.

DISPOSITION_RATIONALE

Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

disposition

REFINE_EVIDENCE_REFRESH_TRIGGER

reason_codes

  1. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

bearer

A backup/rebuild/reconstitution path with state, tools, permissions and a receiving function.

proposition

Possessing a backup does not establish restore capability. A claimed path needs evidence that the required state and function can be reconstituted under the relevant configuration and resource assumptions.

guard_quantifier

Exercise or other adequate evidence should cover the actual claim; refresh is triggered by material changes, stale assumptions or a binding obligation, not by an arbitrary universal frequency.

model_domain

A restoration demonstration establishes the tested path and configuration. It does not establish success under every loss scenario.

mechanism

Challenges accessibility, integrity, compatibility, missing authority and integration before relying on recovery.

consumer_decision

Keep/modify a backup plan, replace it with rebuild, accept loss or schedule a proportionate exercise.

positive_scope

Isolated tests, existing valid demonstrations and cheap deterministic rebuild checks where sufficient.

negative_scope

No production disruption or recurring full rehearsal quota follows from this research.

counterexample

Readable backup bytes cannot restore service when the only decryption credential was lost with the original system.

criterion

Trace what is recoverable, under which loss, how long and with which residual data loss; identify evidence invalidators.

evidence_refs

  1. F008

  2. F017

  3. F043

evidence_ceiling

Scoped current NIST guidance and technical/incident mechanisms; no independent efficacy trial or actual restoration conducted.

remaining_premises

Backup trust, state currency, resource availability, protected authority, dependencies and realistic load.

cheap_path_alternatives

Recreate reproducible stateless artifacts and perform one functional check; use existing current evidence when new testing adds no discrimination.

cost_retirement

Account for storage, credentials, exercise disruption, staff and obsolete formats; retire redundant paths only after protecting remaining obligations.

audit_question

Which specific loss can this path recover from, what evidence exists, and which change would invalidate it?

cases

  1. C04

change_note

Preserves the native anti-backup-theater claim while replacing unconditional periodicity with meaningful freshness and applicable obligations.

Backup job reports success but restore cannot complete, recovered data is inconsistent, required tools/docs are unavailable or the same cause contaminates sources. Current limitation: No production disruption or recurring full rehearsal quota follows from this research.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

Backup job reports success but restore cannot complete, recovered data is inconsistent, required tools/docs are unavailable or the same cause contaminates sources. Current limitation: No production disruption or recurring full rehearsal quota follows from this research.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

Backup trust, state currency, resource availability, protected authority, dependencies and realistic load.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.

CONTROL

Challenges accessibility, integrity, compatibility, missing authority and integration before relying on recovery.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodeled combinations, dependence, observation gaps and changed conditions remain possible. A valid bounded containment contribution need not establish diagnosis or complete restoration.

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

false

PROFILE_TYPE

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE

REASON

The property does not itself claim redundancy benefit; any redundant implementation must invoke ERM-P008/ERM-P009.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

false

PROFILE_TYPE

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE

REASON

The candidate is not a diagnostic claim; outcome observation may still be required by its evidence profile.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Backup, restore and reconstitution paths must be exercised and validated

INITIATING_FAILURE

Backup job reports success but restore cannot complete, recovered data is inconsistent, required tools/docs are unavailable or the same cause contaminates sources. Current limitation: No production disruption or recurring full rehearsal quota follows from this research.

RECOVERY_ACTION

Challenges accessibility, integrity, compatibility, missing authority and integration before relying on recovery.

AUTHORITY_SOURCE

State/configuration identity and the actual authority relevant to the action or claim. A pure model has no external action authority; a bounded internal restore does not by itself establish authority to resume a wider service.

CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE

Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.

RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND

State/data loss bound where the function depends on preserved state; explicitly state a nontrigger for stateless or directly reconstructible functions.

RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND

The declared restoration interval or bound, if the claim requires one. Distinguish detection, waiting, logistics, repair and validation and avoid summing overlapping intervals.

STATE_RECONCILIATION

Reconcile the state required by the named restored function. Broader divergent or external state may remain an explicit residual; authoritative wider service requires its own relevant conditions.

FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS

Restore required data/state and application function to a trusted, current-enough configuration within RPO/RTO and consequence limits. Current scope: Isolated tests, existing valid demonstrations and cheap deterministic rebuild checks where sufficient.

DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS

Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.

DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS

Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.

VALIDATION

An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.

RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY

Keep proof of the postcondition separate from actual permission to resume consequential service. Name the relevant decision maker or rule when applicable.

ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK

A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.

MATURE_FORM

Possessing a backup does not establish restore capability. A claimed path needs evidence that the required state and function can be reconstituted under the relevant configuration and resource assumptions. Guard: Exercise or other adequate evidence should cover the actual claim; refresh is triggered by material changes, stale assumptions or a binding obligation, not by an arbitrary universal frequency.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Backup, restore and reconstitution paths must be exercised and validated

CLAIM

Possessing a backup does not establish restore capability. A claimed path needs evidence that the required state and function can be reconstituted under the relevant configuration and resource assumptions. Guard: Exercise or other adequate evidence should cover the actual claim; refresh is triggered by material changes, stale assumptions or a binding obligation, not by an arbitrary universal frequency.

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Keep/modify a backup plan, replace it with rebuild, accept loss or schedule a proportionate exercise.

CHEAP_PATH

Recreate reproducible stateless artifacts and perform one functional check; use existing current evidence when new testing adds no discrimination.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

Readable backup bytes cannot restore service when the only decryption credential was lost with the original system.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.

MATURE_FORM

Possessing a backup does not establish restore capability. A claimed path needs evidence that the required state and function can be reconstituted under the relevant configuration and resource assumptions. Guard: Exercise or other adequate evidence should cover the actual claim; refresh is triggered by material changes, stale assumptions or a binding obligation, not by an arbitrary universal frequency.

profile_scope

The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

Fast restoration versus backup integrity, freshness and reconstitution validation.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate backup, restore and reconstitution paths must be exercised and validated? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - Does recovery close on independently checked required function, state and dependency postconditions rather than process restart or procedure completion? - What population, denominator, model, confidence, censoring rule and expiry condition bound the reliability claim?

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P018

PROPERTY_NAME

Conditional validity of retry, restart, rollback and checkpoint recovery

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Recovery blocks, checkpoint/restart, transaction rollback and high-availability operations.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. FAULT_TOLERANT_COMPUTING_LINEAGE

  2. SOFTWARE_RELIABILITY_LINEAGE

  3. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION

  4. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. FAULT_TOLERANCE_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

  2. DOMAIN_TRANSLATION

  3. HYBRID_RESOLUTION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Retry a failed operation, restart the process, roll back the version or resume from a checkpoint.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Recovery primitives are beneficial for transient/local faults but amplify overload, repeat deterministic faults or restore inconsistent state when assumptions fail.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Complete the intended operation or restore service/state without duplicate side effects, overload, corruption or recurrence.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Retry storm, non-idempotent duplicate, domino rollback, stale checkpoint, incompatible rollback, restart loop or hidden dependency failure.

MECHANISM

Classify fault transience; bound retries/backoff; establish idempotency; coordinate checkpoints; validate rollback compatibility; circuit-break and escalate.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Transient faults, process crashes, failed releases or recoverable state loss where operation semantics and state are known.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Do not retry deterministic validation errors or overload; fail clearly and preserve evidence.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Idempotency/deduplication, state consistency, checkpoint freshness, dependency capacity, rollback artefacts and stop conditions.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

Credible failure-domain independence, common-cause analysis, standby condition, switchover coverage and state compatibility.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Shortens restoration for the subset of failures these primitives actually cover.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Service owner, operator, recovery controller and users.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Retries increase load; checkpoint overhead; uncoordinated state; old schema cannot roll back; automated loop destroys evidence.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Recovery primitives can mask design defects and create correlated cascades; their success rate is workload- and fault-specific.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Unconditional restart evolved toward bounded, idempotent, state-aware recovery with escalation and postcondition validation.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A fault-class-specific recovery policy with bounded attempts, consistency/compatibility proof, load protection, observation and fallback.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A restart button, retry library or checkpoint file is not the property; valid semantics and successful postconditions are.

reason_codes

  1. NEW_EVIDENCE

  2. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

bearer

A retry, restart, rollback, failover or checkpoint mechanism for a specified fault class.

proposition

Recovery primitives work under different guards; their local success does not establish that external side effects are undone or that repeated attempts remain beneficial under load.

guard_quantifier

A retry needs a recoverable failure and acceptable repeat semantics; rollback needs a compatible retained state; checkpoint restart needs enough recoverable state and handling of external effects. Guard each mechanism independently.

model_domain

An algorithm's state transition can be verified at its abstraction boundary; infrastructure capacity, irreversible actions and external contracts remain separate.

mechanism

Changes execution state, input timing or chosen alternative to escape a fault manifestation.

consumer_decision

Retry, switch algorithm/path, restart, roll back, repair forward or fail clearly.

positive_scope

Bounded automatic/manual recovery and partial internal restoration without root-cause knowledge.

negative_scope

No universal no-retry-on-overload theorem: a controlled later attempt can be useful after load changes. Unbounded immediate retries during overload can worsen it.

counterexample

C10raises90arrivals/s to108attempts/s against100capacity; C14's weak acceptance check can accept a wrong result; C04retains external failure.

criterion

Name the fault, state boundary, repeat/rollback semantics, resource effect, failure of the recovery mechanism and fallback.

remaining_premises

cheap_path_alternatives

One transparent failure, replacement or manual repair can be better than automatic repeated work.

cost_retirement

Recovery logic increases complexity, load and diagnostic masking; retire retries or fallbacks whose rescue set no longer justifies them.

audit_question

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Conditional validity of retry, restart, rollback and checkpoint recovery

INITIATING_FAILURE

Retry storm, non-idempotent duplicate, domino rollback, stale checkpoint, incompatible rollback, restart loop or hidden dependency failure. Current limitation: No universal no-retry-on-overload theorem: a controlled later attempt can be useful after load changes. Unbounded immediate retries during overload can worsen it.

RECOVERY_ACTION

Changes execution state, input timing or chosen alternative to escape a fault manifestation.

AUTHORITY_SOURCE

State/configuration identity and the actual authority relevant to the action or claim. A pure model has no external action authority; a bounded internal restore does not by itself establish authority to resume a wider service.

CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE

Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.

RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND

State/data loss bound where the function depends on preserved state; explicitly state a nontrigger for stateless or directly reconstructible functions.

RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND

The declared restoration interval or bound, if the claim requires one. Distinguish detection, waiting, logistics, repair and validation and avoid summing overlapping intervals.

STATE_RECONCILIATION

Reconcile the state required by the named restored function. Broader divergent or external state may remain an explicit residual; authoritative wider service requires its own relevant conditions.

FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS

Complete the intended operation or restore service/state without duplicate side effects, overload, corruption or recurrence. Current scope: Bounded automatic/manual recovery and partial internal restoration without root-cause knowledge.

DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS

Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.

DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS

Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.

VALIDATION

An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.

RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY

Keep proof of the postcondition separate from actual permission to resume consequential service. Name the relevant decision maker or rule when applicable.

ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK

A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.

MATURE_FORM

Recovery primitives work under different guards; their local success does not establish that external side effects are undone or that repeated attempts remain beneficial under load. Guard: A retry needs a recoverable failure and acceptable repeat semantics; rollback needs a compatible retained state; checkpoint restart needs enough recoverable state and handling of external effects. Guard each mechanism independently.

POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY

Rapid retry/restart versus overload, duplicate effects and corrupt-state recurrence.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate conditional validity of retry, restart, rollback and checkpoint recovery? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - Are the supposed redundant channels actually separate failure domains, and is detection, switchover, state transfer and degraded capacity covered? - Does recovery close on independently checked required function, state and dependency postconditions rather than process restart or procedure completion?

current_audit_questions

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P019

PROPERTY_NAME

Repairability and maintainability by design

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Post-war maintainability programmes, maintainability prediction/demonstration and modular field replacement.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MAINTAINABILITY_LINEAGE

  2. AVAILABILITY_AND_REPAIRABLE_SYSTEMS_LINEAGE

  3. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. MAINTAINABILITY_NATIVE

  2. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  3. CONVERGENT_PROPERTY

ORIGINAL_FORM

Reduce mean corrective maintenance time through modularity, accessibility and standard repair tasks.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

A reliable design can impose unacceptable downtime or recurring error because faults cannot be isolated, accessed, repaired or verified in the field.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Restore the defined function safely within the total downtime bound under actual field support conditions.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Procedure exists but access, isolation, tools, spares, skills, state/configuration transfer or verification make repair infeasible or error-prone.

MECHANISM

Design for access, isolation, modular replacement, test points, diagnostics, standard interfaces, safe handling, configuration/state transfer and repair verification.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Repairable/high-value/long-life systems, remote sites, tight restoration bounds, repeated service intervention or obsolescence exposure.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

For low-cost short-life items, replacement or graceful discard may dominate elaborate repairability.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Maintenance concept, field observations, human factors, logistics, tools, documentation, configuration control and testability.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Reduces active repair and error while making reliability growth and lifecycle support feasible.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Maintainer, operator, logistics owner, asset owner and service user.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Modularity moves complexity to interfaces; inaccessible fasteners; ambiguous connectors; replacement loses calibration/state; “no fault found.”

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Optimising predicted MTTR can ignore diagnosis, logistics and validation; modularity can add failure points.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Task-time prediction evolved toward maintainability-by-design, testability, software operability, remote support and total restoration burden.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Field-demonstrated restoration capability spanning detection, access, repair/replacement, configuration/state preservation, validation and return to service.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A maintainability prediction is not the property; repair performed correctly under real support constraints is.

Procedure exists but access, isolation, tools, spares, skills, state/configuration transfer or verification make repair infeasible or error-prone.

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

LATENT_CONDITION

PROPERTY

TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES

Procedure exists but access, isolation, tools, spares, skills, state/configuration transfer or verification make repair infeasible or error-prone.

OBSERVABLES

Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.

DETECTION_COVERAGE

Coverage is stated for an enumerated fault/failure population, operating mode and latency window.

FALSE_ALARM_COST

Unnecessary maintenance, failover, shutdown, operator load or customer disruption.

MISSED_DETECTION_COST

Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.

ISOLATION_RESOLUTION

Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.

Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.

LATENCY

Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.

CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION

Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.

OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION

Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.

RECOVERY_COVERAGE

A detected fault counts only if the prescribed action restores or contains the target failure with known coverage.

PROPERTY

Repairability and maintainability by design

INITIATING_FAILURE

Procedure exists but access, isolation, tools, spares, skills, state/configuration transfer or verification make repair infeasible or error-prone.

RECOVERY_ACTION

Design for access, isolation, modular replacement, test points, diagnostics, standard interfaces, safe handling, configuration/state transfer and repair verification.

AUTHORITY_SOURCE

The designated current configuration/state authority and authorised operator or controller.

CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE

Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.

RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND

Explicit allowed state/data loss or “none” for state-continuous functions.

RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND

Explicit time-to-restoration bound including diagnosis, logistics, repair and validation.

STATE_RECONCILIATION

Resolve divergent, stale, partial or replayed state before authoritative service resumes.

FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS

Restore the defined function safely within the total downtime bound under actual field support conditions.

DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS

Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.

DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS

Critical dependencies and capacity are verified rather than assumed from local restart.

VALIDATION

Independent end-to-end functional and state checks under representative demand.

RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY

Named human or automated authority with explicit acceptance criteria.

ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK

A bounded fallback when restoration validation fails or the original cause persists.

MATURE_FORM

Field-demonstrated restoration capability spanning detection, access, repair/replacement, configuration/state preservation, validation and return to service.

reason_codes

  1. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

bearer

The maintainability of an item under stated access, procedure, skill and resource conditions.

proposition

Design can make diagnosis, access, repair/replacement and validation easier, but predicted or intrinsic maintainability is distinct from demonstrated restoration by an actual support organization.

guard_quantifier

Bind a repair-time or effort claim to the task, configuration, environment, tools and personnel conditions. Modularity is useful only when its restoration benefit exceeds added interfaces and burden.

model_domain

A design-level task decomposition is a proposal; measured time distributions require representative maintenance observations.

mechanism

Access, replaceable boundaries, testability and retained state reduce selected restoration tasks or uncertainty.

consumer_decision

Repair versus replace, interface design, service tooling, training or graceful discard.

positive_scope

Designed repairability, bounded local demonstrations and actual field capability as separately labelled levels.

negative_scope

No universal claim that modularity or automation shortens total downtime; no inferred human competence from a procedure.

counterexample

A module swaps in minutes but diagnosis, credential acquisition and validation dominate the outage; added connectors create failures absent in a simpler sealed item.

criterion

Compare the complete restoration task and its uncertainties, including maintenance-induced faults, under the stated resources.

evidence_refs

  1. F007

  2. F023

  3. F046

  4. F026

evidence_ceiling

Current publisher scope, primary maintenance guidance and historical operating account; paid IEC clauses and a new maintainability trial are not claimed.

remaining_premises

Physical/software access, real skills/tools, compatibility, diagnosis and post-repair observations.

cheap_path_alternatives

Replacement, graceful discard or a simple known repair can dominate elaborate modularity for low-cost/short-life items.

cost_retirement

Count interface failures, spares, documentation, training and obsolescence over the life cycle.

audit_question

Is this a design promise or demonstrated support capability, and which tasks and conditions determine the full restoration burden?

cases

  1. C04

  2. C05

change_note

Separates native field-demonstrated mature form from valid but weaker design-level evidence instead of rejecting either.

PROPERTY

Repairability and maintainability by design

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

Procedure exists but access, isolation, tools, spares, skills, state/configuration transfer or verification make repair infeasible or error-prone. Current limitation: No universal claim that modularity or automation shortens total downtime; no inferred human competence from a procedure.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

Procedure exists but access, isolation, tools, spares, skills, state/configuration transfer or verification make repair infeasible or error-prone. Current limitation: No universal claim that modularity or automation shortens total downtime; no inferred human competence from a procedure.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

Physical/software access, real skills/tools, compatibility, diagnosis and post-repair observations.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.

CONTROL

Access, replaceable boundaries, testability and retained state reduce selected restoration tasks or uncertainty.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodeled combinations, dependence, observation gaps and changed conditions remain possible. A valid bounded containment contribution need not establish diagnosis or complete restoration.
