PROPERTY

Repairability and maintainability by design

TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES

Procedure exists but access, isolation, tools, spares, skills, state/configuration transfer or verification make repair infeasible or error-prone. Current limitation: No universal claim that modularity or automation shortens total downtime; no inferred human competence from a procedure.

OBSERVABLES

Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.

DETECTION_COVERAGE

Coverage is stated for an enumerated fault/failure population, operating mode and latency window.

FALSE_ALARM_COST

Unnecessary maintenance, failover, shutdown, operator load or customer disruption.

MISSED_DETECTION_COST

Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.

ISOLATION_RESOLUTION

Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.

AMBIGUITY_GROUPS

Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.

LATENCY

Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.

CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION

Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.

OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION

Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.

RECOVERY_COVERAGE

Count a detected event as successfully restored or contained only for the separately declared action outcome and denominator. A true detected event remains detected even when restoration is absent or unresolved. Detection, isolation, containment and restoration coverage are reported separately.

MATURE_FORM

Design can make diagnosis, access, repair/replacement and validation easier, but predicted or intrinsic maintainability is distinct from demonstrated restoration by an actual support organization. Guard: Bind a repair-time or effort claim to the task, configuration, environment, tools and personnel conditions. Modularity is useful only when its restoration benefit exceeds added interfaces and burden.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Repairability and maintainability by design

INITIATING_FAILURE

Procedure exists but access, isolation, tools, spares, skills, state/configuration transfer or verification make repair infeasible or error-prone. Current limitation: No universal claim that modularity or automation shortens total downtime; no inferred human competence from a procedure.

RECOVERY_ACTION

Access, replaceable boundaries, testability and retained state reduce selected restoration tasks or uncertainty.

AUTHORITY_SOURCE

State/configuration identity and the actual authority relevant to the action or claim. A pure model has no external action authority; a bounded internal restore does not by itself establish authority to resume a wider service.

CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE

Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.

RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND

State/data loss bound where the function depends on preserved state; explicitly state a nontrigger for stateless or directly reconstructible functions.

RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND

The declared restoration interval or bound, if the claim requires one. Distinguish detection, waiting, logistics, repair and validation and avoid summing overlapping intervals.

STATE_RECONCILIATION

Reconcile the state required by the named restored function. Broader divergent or external state may remain an explicit residual; authoritative wider service requires its own relevant conditions.

FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS

Restore the defined function safely within the total downtime bound under actual field support conditions. Current scope: Designed repairability, bounded local demonstrations and actual field capability as separately labelled levels.

DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS

Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.

DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS

Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.

VALIDATION

An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.

RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY

Keep proof of the postcondition separate from actual permission to resume consequential service. Name the relevant decision maker or rule when applicable.

ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK

A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.

MATURE_FORM

Design can make diagnosis, access, repair/replacement and validation easier, but predicted or intrinsic maintainability is distinct from demonstrated restoration by an actual support organization. Guard: Bind a repair-time or effort claim to the task, configuration, environment, tools and personnel conditions. Modularity is useful only when its restoration benefit exceeds added interfaces and burden.

Modular replaceability versus interface/configuration/state complexity.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate repairability and maintainability by design? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - Which enumerated failures can the diagnostic detect and isolate within the required latency, and what are the false-positive and false-negative costs? - Does recovery close on independently checked required function, state and dependency postconditions rather than process restart or procedure completion?

current_audit_questions

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P020

PROPERTY_NAME

Supportability, logistics and operational maintenance capability

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Integrated logistics support, operational availability and current IEC supportability practice.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MAINTAINABILITY_LINEAGE

  2. AVAILABILITY_AND_REPAIRABLE_SYSTEMS_LINEAGE

  3. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. MAINTAINABILITY_NATIVE

  2. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  3. HYBRID_RESOLUTION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Provision spares, tools, manuals, trained maintainers and maintenance facilities to meet downtime targets.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

A maintainable design remains unavailable because diagnosis, administration, transport, spares, credentials, tools, documentation or personnel are delayed.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

The complete support system restores required function within the operational downtime bound across deployed locations and mission conditions.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Low bench repair time is overwhelmed by waiting, access, approval, supplier lead time, obsolete parts, unavailable expertise or incompatible configuration.

MECHANISM

Model and measure total downtime; provision/position resources; exercise escalation; manage obsolescence; sustain documentation, credentials and skills.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Distributed fleets, remote/contested sites, long-life assets, supplier concentration, strict availability or disaster recovery.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

For low-criticality items, accept longer restoration or stock simple replacements rather than build a complex support network.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Demand rates, repair-level policy, supply data, workforce readiness, transport/access, contracts, configuration and obsolescence monitoring.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Aligns achieved/operational availability with real support conditions rather than inherent design promises.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Fleet/asset owner, logistics organisation, operator, maintainer and mission planner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Paper spares; wrong revision; expired credentials; inaccessible facility; unsupported dependency; concentrated specialist; supply disruption.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Stocking and spare capacity are costly; forecasts are uncertain; overprovisioning can create obsolescence and maintenance burden.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Spares provisioning broadened to lifecycle supportability, digital/software dependencies, remote operations and obsolescence management.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A tested support concept with total-downtime data, resource/configuration identity, alternatives and explicit risk acceptance for uncovered sites/times.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A logistics plan or SLA is not the property; actual timely access to the right resources is.

EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE

Meta’s secure physical access delayed repair; GitLab relied on slower infrastructure in another region; both show logistics/access are reliability mechanisms (SRC-059, SRC-060).

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

High reliability or local repairability can reduce support demand, but does not eliminate the need to validate residual support assumptions.

OPEN_QUESTIONS

The complete support system restores required function within the operational downtime bound across deployed locations and mission conditions.

OPERATING_PROFILE

Declared demands, workload mix, duty cycle, mode changes and maintenance states.

ENVIRONMENT

FAILURE_DEFINITION

Low bench repair time is overwhelmed by waiting, access, approval, supplier lead time, obsolete parts, unavailable expertise or incompatible configuration.

DEGRADED_ACCEPTABLE_STATE

Only states explicitly accepted by mission/consumer criteria; otherwise none.

MISSION_TIME_OR_DEMAND

CONSUMER

CHEAP_PATH

APPLICABLE

PROPERTY

Supportability, logistics and operational maintenance capability

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

Low bench repair time is overwhelmed by waiting, access, approval, supplier lead time, obsolete parts, unavailable expertise or incompatible configuration.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

Low bench repair time is overwhelmed by waiting, access, approval, supplier lead time, obsolete parts, unavailable expertise or incompatible configuration.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

Demand rates, repair-level policy, supply data, workforce readiness, transport/access, contracts, configuration and obsolescence monitoring.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Outcome- or function-relevant observation, not a component heartbeat alone.

CONTROL

Model and measure total downtime; provision/position resources; exercise escalation; manage obsolescence; sustain documentation, credentials and skills.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodelled combinations, dependence, coverage gaps and changed configuration remain.

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

PROPERTY

Supportability, logistics and operational maintenance capability

INITIATING_FAILURE

Low bench repair time is overwhelmed by waiting, access, approval, supplier lead time, obsolete parts, unavailable expertise or incompatible configuration.

RECOVERY_ACTION

Model and measure total downtime; provision/position resources; exercise escalation; manage obsolescence; sustain documentation, credentials and skills.

AUTHORITY_SOURCE

The designated current configuration/state authority and authorised operator or controller.

CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE

Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.

RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND

Explicit allowed state/data loss or “none” for state-continuous functions.

RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND

Explicit time-to-restoration bound including diagnosis, logistics, repair and validation.

STATE_RECONCILIATION

Resolve divergent, stale, partial or replayed state before authoritative service resumes.

FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS

The complete support system restores required function within the operational downtime bound across deployed locations and mission conditions.

DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS

Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.

DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS

Critical dependencies and capacity are verified rather than assumed from local restart.

VALIDATION

Independent end-to-end functional and state checks under representative demand.

RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY

Named human or automated authority with explicit acceptance criteria.

ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK

A bounded fallback when restoration validation fails or the original cause persists.

MATURE_FORM

A tested support concept with total-downtime data, resource/configuration identity, alternatives and explicit risk acceptance for uncovered sites/times.

reason_codes

bearer

A support system supplying maintenance capability at specified sites and times.

proposition

Restoration depends on available people, spares, tools, information and authority as well as the item's repairability; the scope of supported operation must state those resource conditions.

guard_quantifier

For the asserted mission/site/time, examine whether required resources can arrive and act within the needed window. Do not infer capability from staffing counts or policy existence.

model_domain

Resource availability and scheduling may be modeled; actual access, competence and logistics need observations.

mechanism

Reduces waiting and coordination delays or provides a substitute repair/rebuild path.

consumer_decision

Stock a spare, arrange support, accept longer downtime or reduce the protected mission.

positive_scope

Local resource inventories and tested support paths, including bounded manual alternatives.

negative_scope

No universal overprovisioning target or requirement for an elaborate support network.

counterexample

A technically repairable system remains unavailable because the sole specialist, spare, tool license or recovery credential is absent.

criterion

Distinguish active repair from waiting, diagnose overlapping intervals, and identify which shortages can block the receiving function.

evidence_refs

  1. F023

  2. F006

  3. F033

  4. F026

evidence_ceiling

Scoped normative guidance and historical evidence; no staffing productivity, fatigue or agent performance was measured.

remaining_premises

Site/time coverage, shared-demand correlation, inventory quality, authority and restoration validation.

cheap_path_alternatives

A cheap replacement, an accepted restoration delay or a smaller supported scope may be adequate.

cost_retirement

Inventory ages, trained staff turn over and support itself needs maintenance; remove obsolete stock/support duties deliberately.

audit_question

Which resource can become the restoration bottleneck, over what sites/times, and what happens when several failures demand it together?

cases

Retains native supportability while preventing paper support concepts from earning operational capability.

OPERATING_PROFILE

ENVIRONMENT

FAILURE_DEFINITION

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Supportability, logistics and operational maintenance capability

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

Low bench repair time is overwhelmed by waiting, access, approval, supplier lead time, obsolete parts, unavailable expertise or incompatible configuration. Current limitation: No universal overprovisioning target or requirement for an elaborate support network.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

Low bench repair time is overwhelmed by waiting, access, approval, supplier lead time, obsolete parts, unavailable expertise or incompatible configuration. Current limitation: No universal overprovisioning target or requirement for an elaborate support network.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

Site/time coverage, shared-demand correlation, inventory quality, authority and restoration validation.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.

CONTROL

Reduces waiting and coordination delays or provides a substitute repair/rebuild path.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodeled combinations, dependence, observation gaps and changed conditions remain possible. A valid bounded containment contribution need not establish diagnosis or complete restoration.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Supportability, logistics and operational maintenance capability

INITIATING_FAILURE

Low bench repair time is overwhelmed by waiting, access, approval, supplier lead time, obsolete parts, unavailable expertise or incompatible configuration. Current limitation: No universal overprovisioning target or requirement for an elaborate support network.

RECOVERY_ACTION

Reduces waiting and coordination delays or provides a substitute repair/rebuild path.

AUTHORITY_SOURCE

State/configuration identity and the actual authority relevant to the action or claim. A pure model has no external action authority; a bounded internal restore does not by itself establish authority to resume a wider service.

CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE

Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.

RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND

State/data loss bound where the function depends on preserved state; explicitly state a nontrigger for stateless or directly reconstructible functions.

RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND

The declared restoration interval or bound, if the claim requires one. Distinguish detection, waiting, logistics, repair and validation and avoid summing overlapping intervals.

STATE_RECONCILIATION

Reconcile the state required by the named restored function. Broader divergent or external state may remain an explicit residual; authoritative wider service requires its own relevant conditions.

FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS

The complete support system restores required function within the operational downtime bound across deployed locations and mission conditions. Current scope: Local resource inventories and tested support paths, including bounded manual alternatives.

DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS

Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.

DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS

Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.

VALIDATION

An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.

RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY

Keep proof of the postcondition separate from actual permission to resume consequential service. Name the relevant decision maker or rule when applicable.

ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK

A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.

MATURE_FORM

Restoration depends on available people, spares, tools, information and authority as well as the item's repairability; the scope of supported operation must state those resource conditions. Guard: For the asserted mission/site/time, examine whether required resources can arrive and act within the needed window. Do not infer capability from staffing counts or policy existence.

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate supportability, logistics and operational maintenance capability? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - Does recovery close on independently checked required function, state and dependency postconditions rather than process restart or procedure completion?

PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P021

PROPERTY_NAME

Maintenance-induced failure and maintenance human factors as system mechanisms

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Field maintenance experience, RCM, human-factors programmes and common-cause analysis.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MAINTAINABILITY_LINEAGE

  2. FAILURE_ANALYSIS_LINEAGE

  3. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. MAINTAINABILITY_NATIVE

  2. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  3. CONVERGENT_PROPERTY

ORIGINAL_FORM

Record maintenance error as a cause category and improve procedures/training.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Inspection, calibration, replacement, access, configuration or repair can introduce faults, disable redundancy or create shared misconfiguration.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Maintenance must preserve or restore the required function without creating a new latent, common-cause or interface failure.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Wrong part/configuration, omitted step, damage during access, common calibration error, simultaneous channel disablement or ineffective verification.

MECHANISM

Design out error opportunities; control configuration; isolate channels; use usable procedures/tools; manage fatigue/communication; verify function after work; learn without individual blame substitution.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Intrusive maintenance, repeated “no fault found,” common-channel work, difficult access, night/remote work, complex software/configuration changes.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Eliminate unnecessary maintenance or replace a fragile manual step with a simple poka-yoke/functional check where that is safer.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Work-as-done observation, maintainability design, staffing/fatigue controls, independent verification, event reporting and organisational learning.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Reduces recurrence, common-cause exposure and downtime produced by the maintenance system itself.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Maintainer, operator, fleet/service owner and mission authority.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Blame-only investigation; unreadable procedures; undocumented workaround; verifier shares same misconception; work performed on both redundant channels.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

“Human error” can become a residual label that hides design and organisational causes; added checks can create workload and new failure modes.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Person-centred error counting evolved toward design-for-maintenance, organisational conditions, independent verification and work-as-done evidence.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Maintenance treated as an operational mode with its own hazards, dependencies, state transitions, common-cause controls and post-maintenance functional proof.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A sign-off or training record is not the property; reduced error opportunity and verified post-work function are.

EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE

AWS’s event began with an authorised maintenance command whose input removed excess capacity; GitLab’s recovery work accidentally removed the primary data directory (SRC-058, SRC-060).

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

Some maintenance errors are genuinely individual slips, but durable control still requires analysing the conditions and barriers around them.

OPEN_QUESTIONS

Which post-maintenance checks best detect semantic/configuration errors without duplicating the entire mission test?

PROPERTY

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

Wrong part/configuration, omitted step, damage during access, common calibration error, simultaneous channel disablement or ineffective verification.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

Wrong part/configuration, omitted step, damage during access, common calibration error, simultaneous channel disablement or ineffective verification.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

Work-as-done observation, maintainability design, staffing/fatigue controls, independent verification, event reporting and organisational learning.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Outcome- or function-relevant observation, not a component heartbeat alone.

CONTROL

Design out error opportunities; control configuration; isolate channels; use usable procedures/tools; manage fatigue/communication; verify function after work; learn without individual blame substitution.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodelled combinations, dependence, coverage gaps and changed configuration remain.

APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Maintenance-induced failure and maintenance human factors as system mechanisms

TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES

Wrong part/configuration, omitted step, damage during access, common calibration error, simultaneous channel disablement or ineffective verification.

OBSERVABLES

Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.

DETECTION_COVERAGE

Coverage is stated for an enumerated fault/failure population, operating mode and latency window.

FALSE_ALARM_COST

Unnecessary maintenance, failover, shutdown, operator load or customer disruption.

MISSED_DETECTION_COST

Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.

ISOLATION_RESOLUTION

Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.

AMBIGUITY_GROUPS

Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.

LATENCY

Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.

CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION

Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.

OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION

Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.

RECOVERY_COVERAGE

A detected fault counts only if the prescribed action restores or contains the target failure with known coverage.

MATURE_FORM

Maintenance treated as an operational mode with its own hazards, dependencies, state transitions, common-cause controls and post-maintenance functional proof.

reason_codes

  1. NEW_EVIDENCE

bearer

A maintenance/change activity, its technical interfaces and human organizational conditions.

proposition

Maintenance can introduce failures as well as remove them; human actions should be examined as part of the system mechanism rather than used as an unexplained blame category.

guard_quantifier

For a maintenance task, examine misdiagnosis, access, sequencing, tools, permissions and post-change effects. Claims about workload or competence require actual human evidence.

model_domain

A task hazard model identifies possibilities; attribution and frequency require observation and alternative explanations.

mechanism

Changes state or components, sometimes creating shared faults, incorrect configuration or delayed latent failures.

consumer_decision

Simplify or remove an intervention, improve access/error resistance, stage a change or check the resulting function.

positive_scope

Mechanism-focused maintenance analysis and proportionate post-maintenance checks.

negative_scope

No inference that an operator mention proves sole causation, that automation eliminates error, or that human findings measure machine-agent behavior.

counterexample

A common update applied to many healthy systems introduces the same fault; additional manual checks can themselves increase interruption and workload.

criterion

Distinguish action, context, causal hypothesis and observed outcome; test whether removing or simplifying the task protects the function.

evidence_refs

  1. F026

  2. F019

  3. F035

  4. F036

evidence_ceiling

Gray's selected historical operating data, one supplier incident account and current owner programme summaries; no new human study or independent causal attribution.

remaining_premises

Task exposure, reporting completeness, actual working conditions, alternatives and residual responsibility.

cheap_path_alternatives

Remove unnecessary maintenance or use a simple fixture/direct functional check where it addresses the mechanism.

cost_retirement

Account for fatigue, interruption, training and added checking burden without fabricating effect sizes; retire obsolete tasks.

audit_question

What part of this task can create failure, which system conditions enable it, and would a simpler or absent intervention be better?

cases

  1. C05

  2. C08

change_note

Retains native human-factors boundary and explicitly rejects universal operator-blame extrapolation.

DEPENDENCIES

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

LATENT_CONDITION

DETECTION

Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.

TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES

Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.

FALSE_ALARM_COST

ISOLATION_RESOLUTION

Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.

AMBIGUITY_GROUPS

LATENCY

Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.

CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION

Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.

OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION

Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.

RECOVERY_COVERAGE

Count a detected event as successfully restored or contained only for the separately declared action outcome and denominator. A true detected event remains detected even when restoration is absent or unresolved. Detection, isolation, containment and restoration coverage are reported separately.

POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY

Preventive/corrective intervention versus maintenance-induced failure.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate maintenance-induced failure and maintenance human factors as system mechanisms? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - Which enumerated failures can the diagnostic detect and isolate within the required latency, and what are the false-positive and false-negative costs?

[]

current_audit_questions

  1. What part of this task can create failure, which system conditions enable it, and would a simpler or absent intervention be better?

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P022

PROPERTY_NAME

Age-based preventive maintenance only for valid age-related mechanisms

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Replacement theory and scheduled overhaul; narrowed by airline RCM evidence and modern life-data modelling.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. LIFE_DATA_AND_STATISTICAL_RELIABILITY_LINEAGE

  2. MAINTAINABILITY_LINEAGE

  3. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. STATISTICAL_RELIABILITY_ANCESTRY

  2. MAINTAINABILITY_NATIVE

  3. HYBRID_RESOLUTION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Replace or overhaul at a fixed age to avoid wear-out.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Scheduled intervention cannot reduce random/weakly age-related failures and may introduce maintenance faults or waste useful life.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Reduce mission failure or lifecycle consequence by acting before a demonstrable age-related risk rise.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

A convenient age limit is imposed without a dominant wear-out mode, stable age relationship or evidence that overhaul restores resistance.

MECHANISM

Identify failure mechanism and conditional age-risk; estimate survival/uncertainty; compare maintenance-induced risk and cost; verify post-task reliability.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Dominant wear-out, fatigue, corrosion, consumable depletion or legally/physically bounded life with observable age/exposure.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Run to failure, inspect condition or use simple replacement-on-failure when consequence and restoration support permit.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Mechanism-specific life data, exposure rather than calendar age where appropriate, restoration-effect evidence and maintenance quality.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Prevents predictable wear-out while avoiding ritual overhaul of items without useful age limits.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Maintenance planner, asset/fleet owner and mission-risk authority.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Calendar age used instead of cycles/stress; mixture populations; changed materials; overhaul not as-good-as-new; invasive task causes failure.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

The famous RCM pattern proportions are aircraft-specific; they justify mechanism testing, not a universal claim that age never matters.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Universal scheduled overhaul narrowed to mechanism- and consequence-specific age tasks with field-data refresh.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A maintenance interval justified by a causal degradation mechanism, exposure model, uncertainty, task effectiveness and net-consequence comparison.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A preventive-maintenance calendar is not the property; intervention before a validated age-linked risk is.

Nowlan and Heap found multiple age-reliability patterns and set applicability conditions for scheduled rework rather than endorsing universal intervals (SRC-008).

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

OPEN_QUESTIONS

How should sparse field data be pooled across configurations without erasing mechanism differences?

PROPERTY

CLAIM

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Exact hardware, software, data, model, dependency and procedure versions.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Predeclared sampling/censoring, failure scoring, exposure and stopping rules.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage and representativeness are explicit.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Intervals, posterior uncertainty or bounded qualitative confidence; point estimates alone are insufficient.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Claim coverage is limited to tested/observed failure modes, environments and paths.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Maintenance planner, asset/fleet owner and mission-risk authority.

CHEAP_PATH

Run to failure, inspect condition or use simple replacement-on-failure when consequence and restoration support permit.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

Strong wear-out mechanisms and finite-life items provide robust contexts where age-based replacement is retained.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Evidence expires when configuration, profile, environment, support organisation or dependencies materially change.

MATURE_FORM

A maintenance interval justified by a causal degradation mechanism, exposure model, uncertainty, task effectiveness and net-consequence comparison.

DISPOSITION_RATIONALE

Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

disposition

REFINE_POLICY_JUSTIFICATION

reason_codes

  1. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

  2. NEW_EVIDENCE

bearer

An age-based inspection/replacement policy for an item and failure consequence.

proposition

Scheduled age replacement should be justified by its expected consequence under a defensible age/exposure model and task effect, not by a presumed universal wear-out curve.

guard_quantifier

Under a memoryless life with perfect instantaneous renewal and positive planned cost, the illustrated age replacement adds cost without reducing the inherent failure intensity. Other hazards, constraints or conservative uncertainty can justify other policies.

model_domain

Renewal cost rates are conditional on life law, repair quality, duration and costs. Physical mechanism evidence strengthens transport but no universal optimum follows from a fitted shape.

mechanism

Replaces or renews an item before failure when age meaningfully changes exposure; may instead add unnecessary intervention.

consumer_decision

Scheduled maintenance, condition inspection, replacement on failure or an explicit bounded precaution.

positive_scope

Mechanism-supported wear-out policies and carefully declared uncertainty/constraint-based limits.

negative_scope

No universal bathtub, universal RCM age-pattern proportions or universal claim that scheduled maintenance is wasteful.

counterexample

C05's exponential policy costs1.2858versus1per time unit; its selected wear-out model costs.6093versus1.1284. Both comparisons assume instantaneous perfect replacement and invented costs.

criterion

Specify age/exposure, renewal effect, downtime and induced faults, missed-failure consequence and comparator; test sensitivity to uncertain assumptions.

evidence_refs

  1. F023

  2. F001

  3. F002

evidence_ceiling

NASA's documented later RCM uptake and conditional constructed models; original1978report and its aircraft dataset were not freshly read.

remaining_premises

Hazard/age relationship, informative withdrawal, task efficacy, constraints, costs and field correspondence.

cheap_path_alternatives

Run to failure, simple inspection or replacement on failure when consequence and support allow.

cost_retirement

Include planned labor, downtime, new-part defects and disposal; retire an interval whose protected mechanism or benefit no longer exists.

audit_question

What does age change in this item, what does the intervention reset, and what evidence beats a simpler allowed policy?

cases

  1. C05

change_note

Preserves the native rejection of routine age folklore while allowing explicit decision under uncertainty rather than demanding complete causal knowledge.

PROPERTY

Age-based preventive maintenance only for valid age-related mechanisms

CLAIM

Scheduled age replacement should be justified by its expected consequence under a defensible age/exposure model and task effect, not by a presumed universal wear-out curve. Guard: Under a memoryless life with perfect instantaneous renewal and positive planned cost, the illustrated age replacement adds cost without reducing the inherent failure intensity. Other hazards, constraints or conservative uncertainty can justify other policies.

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Scheduled maintenance, condition inspection, replacement on failure or an explicit bounded precaution.

CHEAP_PATH

Run to failure, simple inspection or replacement on failure when consequence and support allow.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

C05's exponential policy costs1.2858versus1per time unit; its selected wear-out model costs.6093versus1.1284. Both comparisons assume instantaneous perfect replacement and invented costs.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.

MATURE_FORM

Scheduled age replacement should be justified by its expected consequence under a defensible age/exposure model and task effect, not by a presumed universal wear-out curve. Guard: Under a memoryless life with perfect instantaneous renewal and positive planned cost, the illustrated age replacement adds cost without reducing the inherent failure intensity. Other hazards, constraints or conservative uncertainty can justify other policies.

profile_scope

The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY

Scheduled replacement versus induced work, downtime and needless part replacement.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate age-based preventive maintenance only for valid age-related mechanisms? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - What population, denominator, model, confidence, censoring rule and expiry condition bound the reliability claim?

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P023

PROPERTY_NAME

Condition-based and predictive maintenance only with observable precursors and decision value

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

On-condition RCM, machinery condition monitoring, PHM and modern ML/digital-twin predictive maintenance.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. DIAGNOSTICS_AND_PHM_LINEAGE

  2. MAINTAINABILITY_LINEAGE

  3. DOMAIN_SPECIFIC

  4. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. MAINTAINABILITY_NATIVE

  2. STATISTICAL_RELIABILITY_ANCESTRY

  3. DOMAIN_TRANSLATION

  4. HYBRID_RESOLUTION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Inspect a condition indicator before the P–F interval expires or predict remaining useful life to schedule work.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Fixed schedules waste life, but predictions can be uncalibrated, late, false-positive or non-transferable and can trigger harmful maintenance.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Detect actionable degradation with enough lead time and confidence that intervention reduces expected mission/lifecycle loss.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

No stable precursor; sensor drift; domain shift; uncertain RUL ignored; maintenance action ineffective; false alarms dominate; lead time shorter than logistics delay.

MECHANISM

Validate precursor-to-failure relation, sensor chain, uncertainty, lead-time distribution and intervention effect; optimise against simple policies; monitor drift.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Failure mechanisms with measurable deterioration, sufficient lead time, meaningful consequence and an effective intervention.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Use inspection, fixed replacement or run-to-failure when a simple policy performs similarly or data/precursors are inadequate.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Reliable sensing, labelled/field failure data, calibrated uncertainty, domain representativeness, maintenance capacity and action-cost model.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Targets intervention where it can avert failure while reducing needless planned maintenance.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Maintenance planner, asset owner, operator and logistics manager.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Benchmark overfit; synthetic-data gap; leakage; censored labels; black-box confidence; alert fatigue; action changes the data-generating process.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

The literature is heterogeneous and often laboratory/dataset-centric; no evidence supports universal superiority over simpler policies.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Threshold condition monitoring expanded to probabilistic PHM, hybrid physics/data models, uncertainty and decision-aware maintenance.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A field-calibrated, uncertainty-aware precursor and intervention case compared against a cheap baseline under the actual loss function.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A “predictive maintenance” platform or RUL number is not the property; demonstrated earlier/better decisions are.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

OPEN_QUESTIONS

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

LOCAL_EFFECT

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

END_EFFECT

No stable precursor; sensor drift; domain shift; uncertain RUL ignored; maintenance action ineffective; false alarms dominate; lead time shorter than logistics delay.

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

Reliable sensing, labelled/field failure data, calibrated uncertainty, domain representativeness, maintenance capacity and action-cost model.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Outcome- or function-relevant observation, not a component heartbeat alone.

CONTROL

Validate precursor-to-failure relation, sensor chain, uncertainty, lead-time distribution and intervention effect; optimise against simple policies; monitor drift.

RESIDUAL_RISK

PROPERTY

Condition-based and predictive maintenance only with observable precursors and decision value

TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES

No stable precursor; sensor drift; domain shift; uncertain RUL ignored; maintenance action ineffective; false alarms dominate; lead time shorter than logistics delay.

OBSERVABLES

Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.

DETECTION_COVERAGE

Coverage is stated for an enumerated fault/failure population, operating mode and latency window.

FALSE_ALARM_COST

Unnecessary maintenance, failover, shutdown, operator load or customer disruption.

MISSED_DETECTION_COST

Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.

ISOLATION_RESOLUTION

Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.

AMBIGUITY_GROUPS

Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.

LATENCY

Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.

CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION

Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.

OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION

Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.

RECOVERY_COVERAGE

A detected fault counts only if the prescribed action restores or contains the target failure with known coverage.

MATURE_FORM

A field-calibrated, uncertainty-aware precursor and intervention case compared against a cheap baseline under the actual loss function.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Condition-based and predictive maintenance only with observable precursors and decision value

CLAIM

A field-calibrated, uncertainty-aware precursor and intervention case compared against a cheap baseline under the actual loss function.

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Exact hardware, software, data, model, dependency and procedure versions.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Predeclared sampling/censoring, failure scoring, exposure and stopping rules.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage and representativeness are explicit.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Intervals, posterior uncertainty or bounded qualitative confidence; point estimates alone are insufficient.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Claim coverage is limited to tested/observed failure modes, environments and paths.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Maintenance planner, asset owner, operator and logistics manager.

CHEAP_PATH

Use inspection, fixed replacement or run-to-failure when a simple policy performs similarly or data/precursors are inadequate.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

Well-instrumented monotonic degradation with proven intervention can yield strong value; the result remains mechanism-specific.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Evidence expires when configuration, profile, environment, support organisation or dependencies materially change.

MATURE_FORM

A field-calibrated, uncertainty-aware precursor and intervention case compared against a cheap baseline under the actual loss function.

DISPOSITION_RATIONALE

Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

disposition

RETAIN_WITH_DECISION_EVIDENCE

reason_codes

  1. NEW_EVIDENCE

  2. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

bearer

A condition/RUL prediction and the maintenance policy using it.

proposition

Condition-based or predictive maintenance earns a benefit claim through an observable precursor, timely feasible intervention and net consequence compared with an adequate alternative; predictive score alone is insufficient.

guard_quantifier

The precursor and uncertainty must correspond to the deployed population, failure mechanism and decision horizon. Weak evidence can justify an exploratory bounded trial, not a universal superiority claim.

model_domain

Forecast calibration/discrimination and maintenance utility are separate estimands; intervention changes the future data-generating process.

mechanism

Uses earlier information to schedule a beneficial action while avoiding premature or missed maintenance.

consumer_decision

Inspect, repair, schedule replacement, gather labels or retain a simpler baseline.

positive_scope

Laboratory forecasting, validation and field policy evidence as distinct levels.

negative_scope

No automatic transfer of RUL models across machines, duty cycles, sensors or intervention regimes; no universal preference for digital twins/AI.

counterexample

A more sensitive predictor triggers many costly unnecessary replacements for a rare failure and performs worse than a cheap inspection policy.

criterion

Compare full lifecycle and action consequences, calibration at the relevant horizon, lead time and a viable baseline; disclose missing field utility evidence.

evidence_refs

  1. F021

  2. F032

  3. F020

evidence_ceiling

Scoped primary review, current publisher abstract and qualitative NIST workshops; none is treated as a fresh comparative policy trial.

remaining_premises

Representative labels/censoring, precursor stability, available interventions, causal counterfactual, uncertainty and resource cost.

cheap_path_alternatives

Fixed replacement, inspection or run-to-failure may be sufficient or superior; retained uncertainty is legitimate.

cost_retirement

Include sensors, data cleaning, integration, training, drift, spares, false actions and displaced maintenance.

audit_question

Which decision changes because of this forecast, with what lead time and costs, and what evidence establishes benefit over the simplest adequate policy?

cases

  1. C03

  2. C05

change_note

Retains native assumption sensitivity; current2026abstracts broaden discovery but do not upgrade effectiveness evidence.

MISSED_DETECTION_COST

Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.

ISOLATION_RESOLUTION

Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.

AMBIGUITY_GROUPS

Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.

LATENCY

Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.

CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION

Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.

OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION

Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.

RECOVERY_COVERAGE

Count a detected event as successfully restored or contained only for the separately declared action outcome and denominator. A true detected event remains detected even when restoration is absent or unresolved. Detection, isolation, containment and restoration coverage are reported separately.

MATURE_FORM

Condition-based or predictive maintenance earns a benefit claim through an observable precursor, timely feasible intervention and net consequence compared with an adequate alternative; predictive score alone is insufficient. Guard: The precursor and uncertainty must correspond to the deployed population, failure mechanism and decision horizon. Weak evidence can justify an exploratory bounded trial, not a universal superiority claim.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Condition-based and predictive maintenance only with observable precursors and decision value

CLAIM

Condition-based or predictive maintenance earns a benefit claim through an observable precursor, timely feasible intervention and net consequence compared with an adequate alternative; predictive score alone is insufficient. Guard: The precursor and uncertainty must correspond to the deployed population, failure mechanism and decision horizon. Weak evidence can justify an exploratory bounded trial, not a universal superiority claim.

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Inspect, repair, schedule replacement, gather labels or retain a simpler baseline.

CHEAP_PATH

Fixed replacement, inspection or run-to-failure may be sufficient or superior; retained uncertainty is legitimate.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

A more sensitive predictor triggers many costly unnecessary replacements for a rare failure and performs worse than a cheap inspection policy.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.

MATURE_FORM

Condition-based or predictive maintenance earns a benefit claim through an observable precursor, timely feasible intervention and net consequence compared with an adequate alternative; predictive score alone is insufficient. Guard: The precursor and uncertainty must correspond to the deployed population, failure mechanism and decision horizon. Weak evidence can justify an exploratory bounded trial, not a universal superiority claim.

The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P024

PROPERTY_NAME

Closed-loop test–analyse–fix and FRACAS

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Post-war failure reporting, Duane growth, military FRACAS and formal growth-management handbooks.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. RELIABILITY_GROWTH_LINEAGE

  2. FAILURE_ANALYSIS_LINEAGE

  3. MAINTAINABILITY_LINEAGE

  4. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  2. MAINTAINABILITY_NATIVE

  3. HYBRID_RESOLUTION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Record each failure, analyse cause, implement corrective action and track MTBF growth.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Testing and field incidents generate no reliability improvement when failures are merely logged, classified or closed administratively.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Remove or bound recurrent failure mechanisms in the current design/support configuration and verify the changed mission outcome.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Selective reporting; “no trouble found”; delayed fixes; fix not configuration-bound; no retest; curve fit substitutes for causal closure.

MECHANISM

Unique failure identity; exposure/context capture; causal analysis; prioritised design/process correction; independent retest; recurrence monitoring; fleet/configuration propagation.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Development test failures, repeated field events, unexplained downtime, reliability-growth commitments or high-cost maintenance families.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

For isolated low-consequence failures, make the obvious reversible correction and verify function without standing up a heavy FRACAS board.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Data quality, ownership, change authority, configuration traceability, representative retest and recurrence horizon.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Converts failure experience into verified design/support improvement rather than incident accumulation.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Design authority, reliability manager, maintainer, fleet/service owner and acceptance authority.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Ticket closure gaming; duplicate fragmentation; symptom fixes; selective test continuation; unimplemented fleet fixes; no recurrence denominator.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

FRACAS can become labour-intensive bureaucracy and reliability-growth models can reward test selection or delayed fixes.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Failure logs evolved toward configuration-bound causal corrective action, delayed-fix treatment, recurrence families and decision-focused closure.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A proportionate closed loop in which every material failure is tied to exposure, cause confidence, corrective change, verification and recurrence outcome.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

The database or review board is not the property; verified reduction of the causal failure mechanism is.

Closed-loop test–analyse–fix and FRACAS

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

Selective reporting; “no trouble found”; delayed fixes; fix not configuration-bound; no retest; curve fit substitutes for causal closure.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

Selective reporting; “no trouble found”; delayed fixes; fix not configuration-bound; no retest; curve fit substitutes for causal closure.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

Data quality, ownership, change authority, configuration traceability, representative retest and recurrence horizon.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Outcome- or function-relevant observation, not a component heartbeat alone.

CONTROL

Unique failure identity; exposure/context capture; causal analysis; prioritised design/process correction; independent retest; recurrence monitoring; fleet/configuration propagation.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodelled combinations, dependence, coverage gaps and changed configuration remain.

APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Closed-loop test–analyse–fix and FRACAS

CLAIM

A proportionate closed loop in which every material failure is tied to exposure, cause confidence, corrective change, verification and recurrence outcome.

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Exact hardware, software, data, model, dependency and procedure versions.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Predeclared sampling/censoring, failure scoring, exposure and stopping rules.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage and representativeness are explicit.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Intervals, posterior uncertainty or bounded qualitative confidence; point estimates alone are insufficient.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Claim coverage is limited to tested/observed failure modes, environments and paths.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Design authority, reliability manager, maintainer, fleet/service owner and acceptance authority.

CHEAP_PATH

For isolated low-consequence failures, make the obvious reversible correction and verify function without standing up a heavy FRACAS board.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

Growth can plateau or reverse when exposure changes, fixes interact or new complexity is introduced.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Evidence expires when configuration, profile, environment, support organisation or dependencies materially change.

MATURE_FORM

A proportionate closed loop in which every material failure is tied to exposure, cause confidence, corrective change, verification and recurrence outcome.

DISPOSITION_RATIONALE

Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

bearer

proposition

A feedback loop is useful when observations can alter or confirm a specific design, maintenance or acceptance decision and the disposition preserves what is known about exposure and correction.

guard_quantifier

Record a material failure's disposition and supporting evidence at the warranted scale; unresolved causality or accepted risk can be an explicit outcome rather than manufactured closure.

model_domain

Reporting/traceability supports inquiry; a closed loop label does not prove an intervention caused reliability growth.

mechanism

Carries observed failures into candidate cause assessment, targeted change or no action, verification and comparable subsequent observation.

consumer_decision

Fix, investigate, narrow a claim, retain a control, accept a residual or retire unnecessary process.

positive_scope

A one-defect local correction as well as a sustained FRACAS programme.

negative_scope

No board, ticket-volume, universal root-cause or action-change quota.

counterexample

Failure counts decline only because usage falls; closing every ticket does not identify the residual risk.

criterion

Can the reader identify the observed failure, exposure, decision, intervention if any, result and unresolved premises without inferring causality from administrative status?

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Closed-loop test–analyse–fix and FRACAS

CLAIM

A feedback loop is useful when observations can alter or confirm a specific design, maintenance or acceptance decision and the disposition preserves what is known about exposure and correction. Guard: Record a material failure's disposition and supporting evidence at the warranted scale; unresolved causality or accepted risk can be an explicit outcome rather than manufactured closure.

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Fix, investigate, narrow a claim, retain a control, accept a residual or retire unnecessary process.

CHEAP_PATH

Repair an obvious reversible defect and directly verify the function; record a justified no-change disposition.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

Failure counts decline only because usage falls; closing every ticket does not identify the residual risk.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.

MATURE_FORM

A feedback loop is useful when observations can alter or confirm a specific design, maintenance or acceptance decision and the disposition preserves what is known about exposure and correction. Guard: Record a material failure's disposition and supporting evidence at the warranted scale; unresolved causality or accepted risk can be an explicit outcome rather than manufactured closure.

profile_scope

The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P025

PROPERTY_NAME

Corrective-action effectiveness and recurrence control

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

FRACAS corrective-action verification, root-cause analysis and field reliability feedback.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. RELIABILITY_GROWTH_LINEAGE

  2. FAILURE_ANALYSIS_LINEAGE

  3. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  2. CONVERGENT_PROPERTY

ORIGINAL_FORM

Close a problem report after the corrective action passes its verification test.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

A local patch or ticket closure suppresses the symptom while the causal family, sibling configurations or enabling conditions persist.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

The relevant failure family no longer occurs, or its frequency/consequence is demonstrably reduced, across the intended population and configuration.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Fix addresses only one manifestation; test cannot reproduce cause; exposure disappears; sibling systems unpatched; workaround becomes permanent.

MECHANISM

Define recurrence family and causal claim; propagate change; reproduce or challenge mechanism; monitor normalised recurrence and unintended effects.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Repeated incidents, fleet-wide defect, common supplier/configuration, high-severity failure or claimed reliability growth.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

For a simple deterministic defect, a regression/functional test plus configuration deployment proof may suffice.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Failure taxonomy, causal evidence, population/configuration inventory, exposure denominator, change deployment and follow-up period.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Distinguishes real engineering learning from administrative closure and incident-count decline.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Design owner, service/fleet owner, acceptance authority and users exposed to recurrence.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Reclassification; denominator change; silent suppression; partial rollout; collateral regression; long-latency recurrence.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Causal certainty may be unattainable for rare complex failures; monitoring can delay closure indefinitely.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Single-event root cause evolved toward failure-family, system-condition and recurrence-effectiveness tracking.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A bounded causal claim supported by mechanism-targeted tests, deployment evidence and exposure-normalised recurrence surveillance.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A “root cause” field or closed status is not the property; changed recurrence risk is.
