native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P032

PROPERTY_NAME

SLI/SLO and error-budget governance as a scoped decision aid

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Google SRE practice and subsequent industrial adoption/critique.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION

  2. DOMAIN_SPECIFIC

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION

  2. DOMAIN_TRANSLATION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Set an SLO below 100%, measure bad events, and spend the error budget to balance reliability and change velocity.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Teams need an operational threshold linking observed service outcomes to release, stabilisation and alert decisions.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

A user/mission-relevant outcome remains within an agreed loss budget over a declared denominator/window, with action when exhausted.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Easy metric chosen; time/event denominator mismatch; cohort/tail hidden; maintenance excluded; budget treated as permission; chronic exhaustion creates nonsense.

MECHANISM

Select user-relevant SLI; document denominator/window/exclusions; use burn-rate/tail/cohort views; preagree actions; review validity and gaming.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Repeatable online service with measurable consumer outcomes and cross-functional authority to act on budget state.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Use direct incident/change judgement for small or low-volume services where a stable ratio is misleading.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Reliable telemetry, user-journey mapping, stakeholder agreement, release authority, dependency awareness and review cadence.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Creates a common, current decision signal and makes reliability/change trade-offs explicit.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Service owner, product/change authority, on-call and users represented by the SLI.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Nine-count branding; denominator manipulation; omitted cohorts; short/long outage equivalence; chronic debt; threshold chosen backwards from current performance.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Boolean ratios fit request/response better than many other services; correct error-budget response and alert thresholds remain contested.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Uptime targets evolved toward user-focused SLIs, multiwindow burn rates, policy actions and explicit critique of denominator/threshold assumptions.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A revisable, consumer-grounded governance instrument used alongside incident, dependency and tail evidence—not a universal reliability score.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

The SLO dashboard and error-budget ritual are optional; the property is a valid current decision boundary and agreed response.

bearer

A service objective and an authorized policy using its measurement.

proposition

An SLI/SLO and error-budget rule can organize a legitimate service trade-off when measurement, tolerance and decision authority are defined; the ratio itself does not authorize release freezes or other actions.

guard_quantifier

Bind the indicator to a function, denominator/window and accepted objective; state policy exceptions and authority. Aspirational/non-action objectives and small-service direct judgment are valid alternatives.

model_domain

Budget arithmetic is mathematical. The target and action policy are chosen governance, not inferred scientific necessities.

mechanism

Makes an agreed reliability/change trade-off visible and provides a trigger for discussion or action.

consumer_decision

Continue, pause or target changes, revise the objective or use a more suitable measure.

positive_scope

An explicit service policy with known exclusions and supplementary tail/cohort evidence.

negative_scope

No universal five-nines goal, standard20%incident quota, universal production freeze or authority to trade away independent obligations.

counterexample

The aggregate SLO passes while a cohort fails; an error-budget overrun caused by an excluded event can imply different action under different declared policies.

criterion

Inspect denominator, exclusions, data completeness, consumer consequences and who may make the action decision.

  1. F024

  2. F025

evidence_ceiling

Complete Google example policy and scoped implementation guidance; examples are not independent causal effectiveness trials or universally binding rules.

remaining_premises

Good measurement, consumer acceptance, policy authority, business/mission context and distinct safety/security duties.

cheap_path_alternatives

Direct incident/change judgment may be clearer for low-volume or nonservice tasks.

cost_retirement

Measurement and enforcement can create incentives to game windows or classify away failures; retire or revise a policy that no longer serves its consumer.

audit_question

What does the ratio actually measure, what policy follows by whose authority, and what important loss can it hide?

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

SLI/SLO and error-budget governance as a scoped decision aid

CLAIM

An SLI/SLO and error-budget rule can organize a legitimate service trade-off when measurement, tolerance and decision authority are defined; the ratio itself does not authorize release freezes or other actions. Guard: Bind the indicator to a function, denominator/window and accepted objective; state policy exceptions and authority. Aspirational/non-action objectives and small-service direct judgment are valid alternatives.

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Continue, pause or target changes, revise the objective or use a more suitable measure.

CHEAP_PATH

Direct incident/change judgment may be clearer for low-volume or nonservice tasks.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

The aggregate SLO passes while a cohort fails; an error-budget overrun caused by an excluded event can imply different action under different declared policies.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.

MATURE_FORM

An SLI/SLO and error-budget rule can organize a legitimate service trade-off when measurement, tolerance and decision authority are defined; the ratio itself does not authorize release freezes or other actions. Guard: Bind the indicator to a function, denominator/window and accepted objective; state policy exceptions and authority. Aspirational/non-action objectives and small-service direct judgment are valid alternatives.

profile_scope

The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

SLO strictness/reliability protection versus change velocity and useful experimentation.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P033

PROPERTY_NAME

End-to-end health checks and symptom-versus-cause separation

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Built-in test/liveness checks, model-based diagnosis and SRE symptom-oriented monitoring.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. DIAGNOSTICS_AND_PHM_LINEAGE

  2. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION

  3. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. MAINTAINABILITY_NATIVE

  2. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION

  3. HYBRID_RESOLUTION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Poll component liveness and page on unhealthy status.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

A component heartbeat can be green while the actual path is unusable; conversely a symptom can identify impact without establishing cause.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Detect end-to-end functional loss quickly while preserving a separate evidence path for causal diagnosis.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Shallow probe; cached/static response; monitor bypasses dependency/state/authentication; probe shares failure; symptom automatically labelled root cause.

MECHANISM

Use layered probes: end-to-end outcome for impact, component/dependency signals for diagnosis; test probe coverage/failure; validate after recovery.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Remote automated service, failover, load balancer health, readiness/liveness, synthetic transactions or auto-remediation.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

A direct user-visible transaction is often cheaper and stronger than many internal health bits.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Representative journey, safe test account/data, independent monitoring path, timing and known blind spots.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Reduces false-green availability and shortens diagnosis without confusing symptom with mechanism.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

On-call operator, automated traffic manager, incident commander and users.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Probe not representative; synthetic succeeds while cohort fails; health endpoint isolated from data plane; monitor unavailable; causal overreach.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Deep probes can be costly, create load or mutate state; they cannot cover all semantic outcomes.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Single component heartbeat evolved toward layered end-to-end functional monitoring, cohort telemetry and dependency diagnosis.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A documented coverage stack: user/mission outcome detection, diagnostic signals, independent probe health and post-recovery validation.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A green checkmark is not the property; observed required function plus understood coverage is.

CURRENT_STATUS

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROPERTY

EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE

Meta’s DNS servers were operational but unreachable, a direct example of a locally green component and failed service path (SRC-059).

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

No finite set of health checks proves absence of latent or unknown semantic failure.

OPEN_QUESTIONS

How can probe representativeness be continuously estimated as user journeys and dependencies change?

PROPERTY

End-to-end health checks and symptom-versus-cause separation

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

Shallow probe; cached/static response; monitor bypasses dependency/state/authentication; probe shares failure; symptom automatically labelled root cause.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

Shallow probe; cached/static response; monitor bypasses dependency/state/authentication; probe shares failure; symptom automatically labelled root cause.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

DEPENDENCIES

Representative journey, safe test account/data, independent monitoring path, timing and known blind spots.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Outcome- or function-relevant observation, not a component heartbeat alone.

CONTROL

Use layered probes: end-to-end outcome for impact, component/dependency signals for diagnosis; test probe coverage/failure; validate after recovery.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodelled combinations, dependence, coverage gaps and changed configuration remain.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

End-to-end health checks and symptom-versus-cause separation

TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES

Shallow probe; cached/static response; monitor bypasses dependency/state/authentication; probe shares failure; symptom automatically labelled root cause.

OBSERVABLES

Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.

DETECTION_COVERAGE

Coverage is stated for an enumerated fault/failure population, operating mode and latency window.

FALSE_ALARM_COST

Unnecessary maintenance, failover, shutdown, operator load or customer disruption.

MISSED_DETECTION_COST

Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.

ISOLATION_RESOLUTION

Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.

AMBIGUITY_GROUPS

Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.

LATENCY

Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.

CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION

Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.

OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION

Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.

RECOVERY_COVERAGE

A detected fault counts only if the prescribed action restores or contains the target failure with known coverage.

MATURE_FORM

A documented coverage stack: user/mission outcome detection, diagnostic signals, independent probe health and post-recovery validation.

disposition

RETAIN_PROBE_SCOPE

reason_codes

  1. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

  2. NEW_EVIDENCE

bearer

A health probe and the specific function/symptom it observes.

proposition

A functional probe can supply stronger evidence about a named outcome than an internal liveness bit, but neither establishes diagnosis or all service semantics.

guard_quantifier

State what the probe exercises, its own dependencies, observation latency, false results and side effects. An independent path is useful only insofar as it addresses a shared observation failure.

model_domain

Probe pass is an observation conditional on its oracle and coverage; the full semantic requirement may be stronger.

mechanism

Detects end-to-end symptoms and separates them from internal clues used for diagnosis.

consumer_decision

Investigate, contain, repair or retain a simpler check.

positive_scope

Direct local/manual tests and layered monitoring when each layer adds discrimination.

negative_scope

No mandatory monitoring stack or unconditional failover on a failed health signal.

counterexample

A false health-check transition causes unnecessary failover and capacity loss; a sorted-and-same-sum check accepts a nonpermutation.

criterion

Compare the observed predicate with the required function and inspect where both could fail together or the probe could cause harm.

evidence_refs

  1. F017

  2. F043

  3. F009

evidence_ceiling

Operator account, primary design text and an explicit logical counterexample; not a validation of any deployed probe.

remaining_premises

Oracle adequacy, representative transaction, access, probe health, sampling and feasible response.

cheap_path_alternatives

One direct user-visible operation can dominate many internal status bits when it covers the relevant function.

cost_retirement

Deep probes consume load, can mutate state and require credentials; remove duplicates that add no meaningful coverage.

audit_question

Exactly what does this green result prove, what can still be wrong, and can the probe or its response contribute to the outage?

cases

  1. C03

  2. C14

change_note

Preserves the native distinction while treating a layered stack as an optional design, not the universal mature property.

ERM-P033

POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY

No single universal conflict; check local cost, consequence, coupling and competing system objectives.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate end-to-end health checks and symptom-versus-cause separation? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - Which enumerated failures can the diagnostic detect and isolate within the required latency, and what are the false-positive and false-negative costs? - Can the health check remain green while an important user or mission path is unavailable, stale, corrupt or capacity-starved?

current_direction_ids

[]

current_audit_questions

  1. Exactly what does this green result prove, what can still be wrong, and can the probe or its response contribute to the outage?

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P034

PROPERTY_NAME

Explicit dependency, correlation and hidden single-point mapping

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

RBD/FTA serial structures, supply/logistics analysis and modern cloud/service dependency mapping.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. FAILURE_ANALYSIS_LINEAGE

  2. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION

  3. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  2. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION

  3. SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

  4. CONVERGENT_PROPERTY

ORIGINAL_FORM

Represent series/parallel component dependencies in an RBD.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Architecture diagrams omit shared DNS, identity, control planes, libraries, regions, suppliers, spares, people or change channels that dominate failure.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Every dependency necessary for the critical function or its recovery is identified with consequence, alternatives and correlation.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Unknown transitive dependency; fallback uses same provider/control; SLA substitutes for observed performance; human/on-call or logistics bottleneck omitted.

MECHANISM

Discover runtime and organisational dependencies; classify criticality/failure domains; test fallback; record correlated change/maintenance; monitor supplier performance.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

End-to-end service, outsourced/supplier component, multi-region design, recovery plan, shared platform or long logistics chain.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

For simple systems, trace one critical user/mission path and its recovery path rather than build a universal service map.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Telemetry/tracing, contracts plus observed data, architecture and support knowledge, ownership and change notifications.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

Credible failure-domain independence, common-cause analysis, standby condition, switchover coverage and state compatibility.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Exposes serial reliability and common-cause risks that component metrics and nominal redundancy hide.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Architect, service/fleet owner, supplier manager, operator, continuity planner and mission owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Dynamic discovery gaps; shadow dependency; circular fallback; shared credentials; control-plane dependence; concentrated maintainer/supplier.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Maps go stale quickly and can become inventory ceremony; causal dependence is richer than static edges.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Static blocks evolved toward dynamic, transitive, control/state/human/supply dependency and correlated-change models.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A decision-focused dependency model refreshed by telemetry and incidents, including recovery dependencies and credible fallback evidence.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A service map is not the property; knowing which shared dependency can defeat required function and what is done about it is.

EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE

AWS, Meta and CrowdStrike incidents demonstrate storage, backbone/DNS and shared supplier/update dependencies with broad correlated impact (SRC-058, SRC-059, SRC-061, SRC-062).

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

Dependency elimination is impossible; some shared platforms improve reliability through expertise and scale, so the property is visibility and evidence, not universal decentralisation.

OPEN_QUESTIONS

How can hidden control-plane and organisational dependencies be discovered before a failure removes the discovery tools?

reason_codes

  1. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

bearer

A required function and its normal/recovery dependency paths.

proposition

Reliability protection must account for the dependencies actually required during normal operation and recovery, including shared infrastructure that nominal replicas omit.

guard_quantifier

Trace the relevant mission and loss scenario; static edges do not encode timing, capacity, authority or the full joint failure distribution.

model_domain

Series/parallel formulas need valid event semantics and dependence assumptions. A map alone is structural orientation.

mechanism

Reveals hidden single points, shared control/identity and restoration dependence that limit claimed isolation.

consumer_decision

Simplify, isolate, cache, add a compatible fallback or accept the residual.

positive_scope

A focused critical path and recovery path as well as larger justified models.

negative_scope

No claim that all cloud regions/providers always fail together or that a single incident estimates their population reliability.

counterexample

Data-plane copies survive but depend on the same DNS/control-plane planner; internal state returns while external authorization remains unavailable.

criterion

Name each dependency's required role, shared mechanisms, fallback validity and recovery sequencing/capacity.

evidence_refs

  1. F017

  2. F045

  3. F046

evidence_ceiling

One detailed operator report, model exposition and historical definitions; not an independent census of cloud dependencies.

remaining_premises

Actual topology/state, hidden coupling, current configurations, correlated maintenance and fallback behavior.

cheap_path_alternatives

Trace one important consumer path and one restoration path before building a universal map.

cost_retirement

Maps stale and extra providers add coordination/configuration; retire unused edges/controls only after checking remaining consumers.

audit_question

What shared normal or recovery dependency could defeat the claimed protection, and what evidence supports the fallback when it is absent?

cases

change_note

Retains mapping as decision support rather than mandatory inventory ceremony.

MISSION_OR_SERVICE

Every dependency necessary for the critical function or its recovery is identified with consequence, alternatives and correlation. Current scope: A focused critical path and recovery path as well as larger justified models.

OPERATING_PROFILE

ENVIRONMENT

FAILURE_DEFINITION

Unknown transitive dependency; fallback uses same provider/control; SLA substitutes for observed performance; human/on-call or logistics bottleneck omitted. Current limitation: No claim that all cloud regions/providers always fail together or that a single incident estimates their population reliability.

DEGRADED_ACCEPTABLE_STATE

Simplify, isolate, cache, add a compatible fallback or accept the residual.

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

Current limitation: No claim that all cloud regions/providers always fail together or that a single incident estimates their population reliability.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

Unknown transitive dependency; fallback uses same provider/control; SLA substitutes for observed performance; human/on-call or logistics bottleneck omitted. Current limitation: No claim that all cloud regions/providers always fail together or that a single incident estimates their population reliability.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

Actual topology/state, hidden coupling, current configurations, correlated maintenance and fallback behavior.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.

CONTROL

Reveals hidden single points, shared control/identity and restoration dependence that limit claimed isolation.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodeled combinations, dependence, observation gaps and changed conditions remain possible. A valid bounded containment contribution need not establish diagnosis or complete restoration.

CLAIMED_TOLERANCE

The specified number/class of faults tolerated while meeting required function or an accepted degraded state.

FAILURE_DOMAINS

Physical, power, network, control-plane, state, software, supplier, operator and maintenance domains.

INDEPENDENCE_EVIDENCE

Address actual shared causes and the joint event law. Statistical independence is required only by formulas or claims that use it; dependent paths may still provide a positive rescue increment. Copy count or labels alone do not establish separation.

COMMON_CAUSE_COUPLINGS

Specification, design, implementation, environment, supplier, maintenance, configuration and operational coupling.

STANDBY_LATENCY_OR_DORMANCY

Dormant faults, activation delay and cold/warm/hot readiness are measured when applicable.

SWITCHOVER_COVERAGE

Detection, decision, transfer, state synchronisation and post-transfer functional success.

STATE_CONSISTENCY

The takeover state and authority must be current, complete and semantically valid.

DEGRADED_MODE

Declared reduced capability and exit conditions.

TEST_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE

Evidence appropriate to the stated protection claim, including a direct deterministic result or a model at its exact premises where adequate. A general architecture or field-rate claim needs correspondingly broader evidence; no universal live-test or field-study bundle is imposed.

MATURE_FORM

Reliability protection must account for the dependencies actually required during normal operation and recovery, including shared infrastructure that nominal replicas omit. Guard: Trace the relevant mission and loss scenario; static edges do not encode timing, capacity, authority or the full joint failure distribution.

native_id

ERM-P034

POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY

No single universal conflict; check local cost, consequence, coupling and competing system objectives.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate explicit dependency, correlation and hidden single-point mapping? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - Are the supposed redundant channels actually separate failure domains, and is detection, switchover, state transfer and degraded capacity covered?

current_direction_ids

[]

current_audit_questions

  1. What shared normal or recovery dependency could defeat the claimed protection, and what evidence supports the fallback when it is absent?

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P035

PROPERTY_NAME

Hypothesis-bound fault injection and chaos experimentation

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Hardware/software fault injection, dependability validation and 2010s chaos engineering.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. FAULT_INJECTION_OR_CHAOS_TRANSLATION

  2. FAULT_TOLERANT_COMPUTING_LINEAGE

  3. DOMAIN_SPECIFIC

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. FAULT_TOLERANCE_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY

  2. DOMAIN_TRANSLATION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Inject component or service failures to see whether redundancy/recovery works.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Analytical claims about detection, containment, degradation and recovery can remain untested in the integrated current system.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Discriminate a live reliability uncertainty for a specified fault, profile, boundary and decision without causing disproportionate harm.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Random breakage; nonrepresentative fault; weak oracle; no decision consumer; production risk exceeds value; repeated ritual after claim already established.

MECHANISM

State hypothesis/steady-state metric; choose representative fault and blast radius; predefine abort; observe full recovery/postconditions; record decision/update.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Material integrated uncertainty not cheaply resolved by static analysis, simulation, staging or direct functional test.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Use unit/integration test, simulation, replay or nonproduction exercise when it resolves the same uncertainty more safely/cheaply.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Containment, observability, recovery readiness, representative load/state, authorisation, abort/fallback and post-experiment analysis.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Finds integration/coverage gaps and supplies current empirical evidence for specific resilience claims.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Service/mission owner, operator, reliability engineer and change authority.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Toy fault; survivorship; experiment itself causes outage; only steady-state metric checked; no state validation; outcomes not acted upon.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Industrial evidence is advocacy-heavy; systematic review still finds evaluation and adoption gaps; production experimentation creates ethical/operational risk.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Fault injection evolved from component coverage testing toward hypothesis-driven system experiments with blast-radius and decision controls.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A sparse portfolio of claim-bound experiments chosen by expected information value and closed through recovery validation and engineering action.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

“Chaos day,” monkey tooling or periodic failure ritual is not the property; decision-relevant falsification is.

OPEN_QUESTIONS

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

Random breakage; nonrepresentative fault; weak oracle; no decision consumer; production risk exceeds value; repeated ritual after claim already established.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

Containment, observability, recovery readiness, representative load/state, authorisation, abort/fallback and post-experiment analysis.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Outcome- or function-relevant observation, not a component heartbeat alone.

CONTROL

State hypothesis/steady-state metric; choose representative fault and blast radius; predefine abort; observe full recovery/postconditions; record decision/update.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodelled combinations, dependence, coverage gaps and changed configuration remain.

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Exact hardware, software, data, model, dependency and procedure versions.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Predeclared sampling/censoring, failure scoring, exposure and stopping rules.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage and representativeness are explicit.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Intervals, posterior uncertainty or bounded qualitative confidence; point estimates alone are insufficient.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Claim coverage is limited to tested/observed failure modes, environments and paths.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Service/mission owner, operator, reliability engineer and change authority.

CHEAP_PATH

Use unit/integration test, simulation, replay or nonproduction exercise when it resolves the same uncertainty more safely/cheaply.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

A successful experiment proves only the tested conditions; it never establishes general resilience.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Evidence expires when configuration, profile, environment, support organisation or dependencies materially change.

MATURE_FORM

A sparse portfolio of claim-bound experiments chosen by expected information value and closed through recovery validation and engineering action.

DISPOSITION_RATIONALE

Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

bearer

proposition

Fault injection can discriminate a relevant failure/recovery assumption when the fault, workload, configuration, observations and permitted exposure match the question; passing a finite test is bounded evidence.

guard_quantifier

Choose a worthwhile unresolved question, adequate observation and supported containment/return conditions. Justified continuation is a valid outcome. Live production injection is outside this commission.

model_domain

A simulator/model test establishes its model behavior. Operational transfer needs real-system correspondence and separate authorization.

mechanism

Challenges a particular tolerated-fault or restoration claim rather than accumulating exercise counts.

consumer_decision

Correct, narrow, confirm or retire a claim/control, or decide that existing evidence already suffices.

positive_scope

Unit/integration tests, deterministic replay, simulation, isolated exercises and duly authorized production experiments in their own domains.

negative_scope

No mandatory production-only continuous chaos, novelty quota, action-change quota or universal resilience certification.

counterexample

Killing a stateless worker proves little about a latent corrupt-state or shared-control failure; repeating the same easy fault need not add information.

criterion

Name the receiving decision, fault representativeness, stop/recovery conditions, evidence invalidators, cost and cheapest adequate alternative.

cost_retirement

PROPERTY

Hypothesis-bound fault injection and chaos experimentation

REQUIRED_FUNCTION

Discriminate a live reliability uncertainty for a specified fault, profile, boundary and decision without causing disproportionate harm. Current scope: Unit/integration tests, deterministic replay, simulation, isolated exercises and duly authorized production experiments in their own domains.

MISSION_OR_SERVICE

Discriminate a live reliability uncertainty for a specified fault, profile, boundary and decision without causing disproportionate harm. Current scope: Unit/integration tests, deterministic replay, simulation, isolated exercises and duly authorized production experiments in their own domains.

OPERATING_PROFILE

Declared demands, workload mix, duty cycle, mode changes and maintenance states.

ENVIRONMENT

Declared physical, software, organisational and dependency environment.

FAILURE_DEFINITION

Random breakage; nonrepresentative fault; weak oracle; no decision consumer; production risk exceeds value; repeated ritual after claim already established. Current limitation: No mandatory production-only continuous chaos, novelty quota, action-change quota or universal resilience certification.

DEGRADED_ACCEPTABLE_STATE

Only states explicitly accepted by mission/consumer criteria; otherwise none.

MISSION_TIME_OR_DEMAND

Specified interval, number of demands or service-measurement window.

CONSUMER

Correct, narrow, confirm or retire a claim/control, or decide that existing evidence already suffices.

CHEAP_PATH

Use existing current evidence, a focused functional check or nonproduction replay when it resolves the same uncertainty.

MATURE_FORM

Fault injection can discriminate a relevant failure/recovery assumption when the fault, workload, configuration, observations and permitted exposure match the question; passing a finite test is bounded evidence. Guard: Choose a worthwhile unresolved question, adequate observation and supported containment/return conditions. Justified continuation is a valid outcome. Live production injection is outside this commission.

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Hypothesis-bound fault injection and chaos experimentation

INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE

Random breakage; nonrepresentative fault; weak oracle; no decision consumer; production risk exceeds value; repeated ritual after claim already established. Current limitation: No mandatory production-only continuous chaos, novelty quota, action-change quota or universal resilience certification.

LOCAL_EFFECT

Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.

NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT

Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.

END_EFFECT

Random breakage; nonrepresentative fault; weak oracle; no decision consumer; production risk exceeds value; repeated ritual after claim already established. Current limitation: No mandatory production-only continuous chaos, novelty quota, action-change quota or universal resilience certification.

PROPAGATION_PATH

Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY

A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.

DEPENDENCIES

Actual injected-fault relevance, configuration, workload, safety/exposure authority and reliable measurements.

COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING

Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

LATENT_CONDITION

Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.

DETECTION

Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.

CONTROL

Challenges a particular tolerated-fault or restoration claim rather than accumulating exercise counts.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodeled combinations, dependence, observation gaps and changed conditions remain possible. A valid bounded containment contribution need not establish diagnosis or complete restoration.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Hypothesis-bound fault injection and chaos experimentation

CLAIM

Fault injection can discriminate a relevant failure/recovery assumption when the fault, workload, configuration, observations and permitted exposure match the question; passing a finite test is bounded evidence. Guard: Choose a worthwhile unresolved question, adequate observation and supported containment/return conditions. Justified continuation is a valid outcome. Live production injection is outside this commission.

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Correct, narrow, confirm or retire a claim/control, or decide that existing evidence already suffices.

CHEAP_PATH

Use existing current evidence, a focused functional check or nonproduction replay when it resolves the same uncertainty.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

Killing a stateless worker proves little about a latent corrupt-state or shared-control failure; repeating the same easy fault need not add information.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.

MATURE_FORM

Fault injection can discriminate a relevant failure/recovery assumption when the fault, workload, configuration, observations and permitted exposure match the question; passing a finite test is bounded evidence. Guard: Choose a worthwhile unresolved question, adequate observation and supported containment/return conditions. Justified continuation is a valid outcome. Live production injection is outside this commission.

profile_scope

The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

native_audit_unique
native_id

ERM-P035

POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY

Failure-learning value versus production/mission risk and evidence cost.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate hypothesis-bound fault injection and chaos experimentation? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - What population, denominator, model, confidence, censoring rule and expiry condition bound the reliability claim? - Will another fault-injection experiment discriminate a live uncertainty and change a decision, or would it be ceremony?

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P036

PROPERTY_NAME

Overload-aware recovery: capacity margin, load shedding and bounded retries

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Queueing/capacity practice, high-availability service recovery and overload-control patterns.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION

  2. AVAILABILITY_AND_REPAIRABLE_SYSTEMS_LINEAGE

  3. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION

  2. RELIABILITY_ENGINEERING_NATIVE

  3. HYBRID_RESOLUTION

ORIGINAL_FORM

Keep spare capacity, shed low-priority load and retry failed requests.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Failure removes capacity while backlog/retries increase demand, so failover/restart can trigger a second collapse.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Protect priority function and recover without unstable positive feedback or exhaustion of the remaining fault-tolerant capacity.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Retry storm; thundering herd; failover target underprovisioned; cache cold start; load shedding removes critical work; no admission control.

MECHANISM

Reserve margin; classify load; cap/constrain retries; exponential backoff/jitter; circuit break; shed by priority; ramp recovery; test cold/failed capacity.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Elastic/queued services, failover, regional loss, dependency slowdown, mass restart or bursty demand.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Reject clearly and early rather than queue/retry when capacity is exhausted and work is safely repeatable later.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Demand/capacity observability, priority semantics, idempotency, queue limits, fallback and consumer communication.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Prevents recovery mechanisms from amplifying the initiating fault and preserves critical service.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Operator, service owner, priority users and incident commander.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Incorrect priorities; hidden downstream bottleneck; stale capacity estimate; retries across many clients synchronise; shed work not recoverable.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Spare capacity costs money/energy; load shedding can externalise harm and obscure underinvestment.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Static N+1 margin evolved toward dynamic admission, priority shedding, retry budgets and staged reconstitution.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A measured stability envelope and failure-mode-specific overload policy, including consumer consequences and recovery postconditions.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A circuit-breaker library or autoscaler is not the property; stable protected operation under the target loss is.

CURRENT_STATUS

CONTEXT_DEPENDENT

AWS reported backlogs after S3 recovery; Meta explicitly avoided turning all services on at once because caches, power and systems could crash (SRC-058, SRC-059).

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

For non-queued fixed-demand systems this property may not trigger; extra mechanisms can add complexity.

OPEN_QUESTIONS

How should retry/load-shed policies coordinate across independently owned clients and dependencies?

reason_codes

  1. NEW_EVIDENCE

  2. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

bearer

A resource-limited service and its admission/retry/recovery policy.

proposition

Recovery work competes for capacity; retries, failover and backlog replay can turn a partial failure into overload unless their resource effects and consumer priorities are considered.

guard_quantifier

A simple constant-rate fluid model needs arrival work below service capacity for stability; real queues add variability, deadlines, finite buffers and changing capacities.

model_domain

The load inequality is conditional mathematics, not a production retry budget or proof of all tail latency.

mechanism

Limits amplification, reserves useful capacity or sacrifices selected work to permit recovery.

consumer_decision

Backoff, shed load, limit concurrency, disable a harmful retry/failover loop, increase capacity or accept delay.

positive_scope

Measured or conservatively bounded capacity policies with explicit consequence.

negative_scope

No automatic inference that more spare capacity is always economical or that rejecting load is harmless.

counterexample

C10's90requests/s are below100capacity but20%one-retry amplification raises attempts to108; the AWS account describes related recovery/backlog interactions at one event.

criterion

Include normal, retry and recovery work in the load model; check who bears rejection/delay and when the system can drain.

evidence_refs

  1. F017

  2. F043

  3. F024

evidence_ceiling

Operator account and constructed inequality; no queueing performance benchmark or universal overload threshold.

remaining_premises

Service work distribution, current capacity, retry semantics, fallback capacity, deadlines and accepted losses.

cheap_path_alternatives

Reject early or remove an amplifying action when that protects the named function; adding another layer is not automatically necessary.

cost_retirement

Reserve capacity costs energy/resources; avoid permanent controls that merely conceal a removed bottleneck.

audit_question

Can recovery attempts exceed surviving capacity, and which restriction or cheaper response best preserves the authorized function?

cases

  1. C10

  2. C11

change_note

Retains native overload awareness and separates a mathematical stability check from operational optimization.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

PROPERTY

Overload-aware recovery: capacity margin, load shedding and bounded retries

INITIATING_FAILURE

Retry storm; thundering herd; failover target underprovisioned; cache cold start; load shedding removes critical work; no admission control. Current limitation: No automatic inference that more spare capacity is always economical or that rejecting load is harmless.

RECOVERY_ACTION

Limits amplification, reserves useful capacity or sacrifices selected work to permit recovery.

AUTHORITY_SOURCE

State/configuration identity and the actual authority relevant to the action or claim. A pure model has no external action authority; a bounded internal restore does not by itself establish authority to resume a wider service.

CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE

Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.

RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND

State/data loss bound where the function depends on preserved state; explicitly state a nontrigger for stateless or directly reconstructible functions.

RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND

The declared restoration interval or bound, if the claim requires one. Distinguish detection, waiting, logistics, repair and validation and avoid summing overlapping intervals.

STATE_RECONCILIATION

Reconcile the state required by the named restored function. Broader divergent or external state may remain an explicit residual; authoritative wider service requires its own relevant conditions.

FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS

Protect priority function and recover without unstable positive feedback or exhaustion of the remaining fault-tolerant capacity. Current scope: Measured or conservatively bounded capacity policies with explicit consequence.

DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS

Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.

DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS

Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.

VALIDATION

An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.

RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY

Keep proof of the postcondition separate from actual permission to resume consequential service. Name the relevant decision maker or rule when applicable.

ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK

A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.

MATURE_FORM

Recovery work competes for capacity; retries, failover and backlog replay can turn a partial failure into overload unless their resource effects and consumer priorities are considered. Guard: A simple constant-rate fluid model needs arrival work below service capacity for stability; real queues add variability, deadlines, finite buffers and changing capacities.

native_id

ERM-P036

POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY

Spare capacity and load shedding versus cost/efficiency and service completeness.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate overload-aware recovery: capacity margin, load shedding and bounded retries? - Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version? - Does recovery close on independently checked required function, state and dependency postconditions rather than process restart or procedure completion?

current_direction_ids

  1. D-17

  2. D-18

current_audit_questions

  1. Can recovery attempts exceed surviving capacity, and which restriction or cheaper response best preserves the authorized function?

  2. Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?

  3. What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

native_record
PROPERTY_ID

ERM-P037

PROPERTY_NAME

Observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Built-in test/maintenance records, incident logging, flight/industrial recorders and service observability.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. DIAGNOSTICS_AND_PHM_LINEAGE

  2. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_OR_SRE_TRANSLATION

  3. MAINTAINABILITY_LINEAGE

  4. HYBRID

RELATIONSHIP_TO_OTHER_TRADITIONS

  1. MAINTAINABILITY_NATIVE

  2. SERVICE_RELIABILITY_TRANSLATION

  3. CONVERGENT_PROPERTY

ORIGINAL_FORM

Log faults and maintenance actions for troubleshooting and FRACAS.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

The initiating failure or automatic remediation destroys/overwrites telemetry, tools, clocks or state needed to diagnose, validate recovery and prevent recurrence.

REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION

Retain sufficient trustworthy evidence to determine impact, state, likely causes, actions and post-recovery correctness within time/privacy constraints.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Logs share failed control plane; clocks diverge; restart erases state; auto-remediation loops; high volume drops key evidence; recovery contaminates artefacts.

MECHANISM

Independent/remote telemetry paths; durable event/action records; time/identity correlation; bounded snapshots; evidence-preserving recovery mode; privacy/access governance.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Complex automated systems, correlated outages, remote repair, stateful recovery or rare high-consequence events.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

For simple deterministic faults, record the minimal causal/action evidence rather than instrument everything.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Independent power/network/storage where warranted, data quality, clocks, access, retention, privacy and incident procedures.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS

A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.

FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS

A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.

REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS

No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS

Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.

RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS

A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.

MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Shortens diagnosis, supports state reconciliation and allows corrective-action effectiveness to be tested.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Operator, maintainer, incident investigator, design owner and return-to-service authority.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

Telemetry blind spot; observer overload; misleading stale metrics; data loss; sensitive evidence withheld; logs treated as ground truth.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

Observability can be costly, intrusive and security/privacy-sensitive; more data does not guarantee diagnosis.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Fault codes evolved toward distributed traces, event/state provenance, recovery journals and independent evidence channels.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Decision-focused observability resilient to the target failure, with known coverage, integrity, retention and evidence-preserving automation.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A logging stack is not the property; reliable evidence for live decisions and recurrence learning is.

PROPERTY

Observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery

TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES

Logs share failed control plane; clocks diverge; restart erases state; auto-remediation loops; high volume drops key evidence; recovery contaminates artefacts.

OBSERVABLES

Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.

DETECTION_COVERAGE

Coverage is stated for an enumerated fault/failure population, operating mode and latency window.

FALSE_ALARM_COST

Unnecessary maintenance, failover, shutdown, operator load or customer disruption.

MISSED_DETECTION_COST

Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.

ISOLATION_RESOLUTION

Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.

AMBIGUITY_GROUPS

Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.

LATENCY

Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.

CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION

Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.

OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION

Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.

RECOVERY_COVERAGE

A detected fault counts only if the prescribed action restores or contains the target failure with known coverage.

MATURE_FORM

Decision-focused observability resilient to the target failure, with known coverage, integrity, retention and evidence-preserving automation.

DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS

VALIDATION

RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY

Named human or automated authority with explicit acceptance criteria.

ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK

A bounded fallback when restoration validation fails or the original cause persists.

PROPERTY

Observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery

CLAIM

Decision-focused observability resilient to the target failure, with known coverage, integrity, retention and evidence-preserving automation.

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Exact hardware, software, data, model, dependency and procedure versions.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Predeclared sampling/censoring, failure scoring, exposure and stopping rules.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage and representativeness are explicit.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Intervals, posterior uncertainty or bounded qualitative confidence; point estimates alone are insufficient.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Claim coverage is limited to tested/observed failure modes, environments and paths.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Operator, maintainer, incident investigator, design owner and return-to-service authority.

CHEAP_PATH

For simple deterministic faults, record the minimal causal/action evidence rather than instrument everything.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

In some failures independent physical inspection or direct test is more informative than extensive telemetry.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Evidence expires when configuration, profile, environment, support organisation or dependencies materially change.

MATURE_FORM

Decision-focused observability resilient to the target failure, with known coverage, integrity, retention and evidence-preserving automation.

DISPOSITION_RATIONALE

Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

native_id

current_id

DRF-L2-C037

disposition

RETAIN_WITH_INFORMATION_COST

reason_codes

  1. NEW_EVIDENCE

  2. ANALYTICAL_REDECOMPOSITION

bearer

Failure/recovery observations and the decisions they can support.

proposition

Preserving relevant observations can improve later discrimination and correction, including after a recovery that did not diagnose the cause; observation is not itself diagnosis or protected operation.

guard_quantifier

Collect information that remains available under the target failure and is adequate for a named question. Retention and access must respect actual constraints and cost.

model_domain

A log is evidence of recorded observations under a measurement process, not a complete causal history.

mechanism

Retains before/after state, symptoms and actions that recovery may otherwise erase.

consumer_decision

Reproduce a failure, distinguish causes, assess a fix or decide that no further investigation is useful.

positive_scope

Minimal deterministic evidence and richer instrumentation where materially useful.

negative_scope

No log-everything or independent-telemetry-stack requirement; no inferred competence from data volume.

counterexample

A restart restores service but deletes the only symptom trace; conversely, huge logs collected by the failing shared dependency are unavailable during the event.

criterion

Identify each retained signal's question, coverage, integrity/clock assumptions and survival under the target failure.

evidence_refs

  1. F043

  2. F026

  3. F017

  4. F020

evidence_ceiling

Primary designs, historical observations, operator account and qualitative AI guidance; no measured observability effectiveness or privacy assessment.

remaining_premises

Measurement correctness, retention access, clock/order meaning, feasible analysis and accepted collection constraints.

cheap_path_alternatives

Record the minimal reproducer, action and result for a deterministic fault.

cost_retirement

Logging consumes storage, performance, attention and sometimes privacy; retire unused streams and avoid unsupported universal retention periods.

audit_question

Which later decision needs this evidence, can the target failure erase it, and does retaining more data actually improve discrimination?

cases

  1. C12

  2. C14

change_note

Retains native evidence preservation and gives the reverse recovery-to-diagnosis direction a conditional, not automatic, pathway.

Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.

CONTROL

Retains before/after state, symptoms and actions that recovery may otherwise erase.

RESIDUAL_RISK

Unmodeled combinations, dependence, observation gaps and changed conditions remain possible. A valid bounded containment contribution need not establish diagnosis or complete restoration.

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

false

PROFILE_TYPE

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE

REASON

The property does not itself claim redundancy benefit; any redundant implementation must invoke ERM-P008/ERM-P009.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery

TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES

Logs share failed control plane; clocks diverge; restart erases state; auto-remediation loops; high volume drops key evidence; recovery contaminates artefacts. Current limitation: No log-everything or independent-telemetry-stack requirement; no inferred competence from data volume.

OBSERVABLES

Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.

DETECTION_COVERAGE

Coverage is stated for an enumerated fault/failure population, operating mode and latency window.

FALSE_ALARM_COST

Unnecessary maintenance, failover, shutdown, operator load or customer disruption.

MISSED_DETECTION_COST

Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.

ISOLATION_RESOLUTION

Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.

AMBIGUITY_GROUPS

Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.

LATENCY

Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.

CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION

Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.

OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION

Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.

RECOVERY_COVERAGE

Count a detected event as successfully restored or contained only for the separately declared action outcome and denominator. A true detected event remains detected even when restoration is absent or unresolved. Detection, isolation, containment and restoration coverage are reported separately.

MATURE_FORM

Preserving relevant observations can improve later discrimination and correction, including after a recovery that did not diagnose the cause; observation is not itself diagnosis or protected operation. Guard: Collect information that remains available under the target failure and is adequate for a named question. Retention and access must respect actual constraints and cost.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery

INITIATING_FAILURE

Logs share failed control plane; clocks diverge; restart erases state; auto-remediation loops; high volume drops key evidence; recovery contaminates artefacts. Current limitation: No log-everything or independent-telemetry-stack requirement; no inferred competence from data volume.

RECOVERY_ACTION

Retains before/after state, symptoms and actions that recovery may otherwise erase.

AUTHORITY_SOURCE

State/configuration identity and the actual authority relevant to the action or claim. A pure model has no external action authority; a bounded internal restore does not by itself establish authority to resume a wider service.

CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE

Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.

RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND

State/data loss bound where the function depends on preserved state; explicitly state a nontrigger for stateless or directly reconstructible functions.

RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND

The declared restoration interval or bound, if the claim requires one. Distinguish detection, waiting, logistics, repair and validation and avoid summing overlapping intervals.

STATE_RECONCILIATION

Reconcile the state required by the named restored function. Broader divergent or external state may remain an explicit residual; authoritative wider service requires its own relevant conditions.

FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS

Retain sufficient trustworthy evidence to determine impact, state, likely causes, actions and post-recovery correctness within time/privacy constraints. Current scope: Minimal deterministic evidence and richer instrumentation where materially useful.

DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS

Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.

DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS

Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.

VALIDATION

An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.

RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY

Keep proof of the postcondition separate from actual permission to resume consequential service. Name the relevant decision maker or rule when applicable.

ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK

A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.

MATURE_FORM

Preserving relevant observations can improve later discrimination and correction, including after a recovery that did not diagnose the cause; observation is not itself diagnosis or protected operation. Guard: Collect information that remains available under the target failure and is adequate for a named question. Retention and access must respect actual constraints and cost.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE
APPLICABLE

true

PROPERTY

Observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery

CLAIM

Preserving relevant observations can improve later discrimination and correction, including after a recovery that did not diagnose the cause; observation is not itself diagnosis or protected operation. Guard: Collect information that remains available under the target failure and is adequate for a named question. Retention and access must respect actual constraints and cost.

POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR

Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY

Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.

OPERATIONAL_PROFILE

Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN

Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.

MODEL

Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.

ASSUMPTIONS

Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.

CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY

Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.

CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS

Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.

COVERAGE

Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Reproduce a failure, distinguish causes, assess a fix or decide that no further investigation is useful.

CHEAP_PATH

Record the minimal reproducer, action and result for a deterministic fault.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

A restart restores service but deletes the only symptom trace; conversely, huge logs collected by the failing shared dependency are unavailable during the event.

EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS

Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.

MATURE_FORM

Preserving relevant observations can improve later discrimination and correction, including after a recovery that did not diagnose the cause; observation is not itself diagnosis or protected operation. Guard: Collect information that remains available under the target failure and is adequate for a named question. Retention and access must respect actual constraints and cost.

profile_scope

The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.
